docs.title: plots
docs.text:
Techniques that draw figures of cases, courts, panels, and judges.

Each is an amos plot (amos.plots.Plot), so it is added to the amos library when courtpy is imported, can be named in the settings of an "artist" worker, takes the parameters that every plot takes ("width", "height", "title", "style", and so on), and adds its figure to the dataset's figures under its name. Courts are labeled with their "feature_name" in the jurisdiction's table of courts (such as "Tenth Circuit"; see courtpy.courts.court_labels), in the order of the table.

A rate is the share of the cases that have a flag (or the mean of a number), measured from the cases themselves, so it is drawn without a confidence interval. Each bar says how many cases it counts.

Technique Draws Needs court_rates The rate of a column in each court, with the rate of every court as a line. Cases, with the column (the label, unless "column" is set). cases_over_time The number of cases of each court in each year, a panel for each court. Cases, with "year". issues_over_time The number of cases with each issue (a column of flags, such as "criminal_firearm") in each court in each year, a panel for each court. Cases, with "year" and the columns in "issues". panel_composition The rate of a column for each composition of the panel by the parties of the presidents who appointed its judges ("DDD" to "RRR"), split by another column if "by" is set. Cases, with the judges' parties (from add_biography or code_panels). lower_court_rates The rate of a column for each court whose decisions a court reviews, a panel for each reviewing court. Cases, with "lower_court_name" or "lower_court_num". trends_by_administration The yearly rate of a column in each court, a panel for each court, with the terms of Democratic and Republican presidents shaded. Cases, with "year". idb_confusion_matrices A confusion matrix for each variable that the data and the Integrated Database both have, with Cohen's kappa. The table of compare_with_idb. idb_missing_differences The share of each variable among the appeals of the Integrated Database that the data has minus the share among those it lacks, for each circuit or district. The second table of compare_with_idb. judge_network The judges as a network, joined by how often they sat together (or, with "dissents", how often one dissented from the other), colored by party. Votes (see cases_to_votes). Contents

CasesOverTime: the number of cases of each court in each year. CourtRates: the rate of a column in each court. IdbConfusionMatrices: how the data agrees with the Integrated Database, a confusion matrix for each variable. IdbMissingDifferences: how the Integrated Database's appeals that the data lacks differ from those it has, in each group. IssuesOverTime: the number of cases with each issue in each court in each year. JudgeNetwork: the judges as a network of who sat with, or dissented from, whom. LowerCourtRates: the rate of a column for each court below, by the court that reviewed it. PanelComposition: the rate of a column for each composition of the panel by party. TrendsByAdministration: the yearly rate of a column in each court, with the presidents' terms shaded. _DEFAULT_RATE: the column whose rate is drawn when there is no label and none is named. _PARTY_COLORS: the colors of Democratic and Republican appointees and presidents.

def draw(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    year: str = 'year',
    court_name: str = 'court_name',
    court_num: str = 'court_num',
    jurisdiction: str = 'federal',
    columns: int = 4,
    **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Draws the number of cases of each court in each year.

    Args:
        item: the cases.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        year: the column with each case's year. Defaults to "year".
        court_name: the column with courtpy's name for each case's court.
            Defaults to "court_name".
        court_num: the column with courtpy's number for each case's
            court. Defaults to "court_num".
        jurisdiction: the folder of the jurisdiction's table of courts.
            Defaults to "federal".

        **kwargs: not used.

    """
    data = item.data
    counts = _yearly(
        data, pd.Series(1, index = data.index, name = 'cases'),
        year = year, court_name = court_name, court_num = court_num,
        jurisdiction = jurisdiction, how = 'sum')
    panels = _court_panels(figure, counts.index, columns)
    years = counts.columns.to_numpy()
    for court, axes in panels.items():
        axes.plot(years, counts.loc[court].to_numpy(), marker = '.')
    figure.supxlabel('Year')
    figure.supylabel('Cases')

def draw(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    column: str | None = None,
    court_name: str = 'court_name',
    court_num: str = 'court_num',
    jurisdiction: str = 'federal',
    **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Draws the rate of `column` in each court.

    Args:
        item: the cases.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        column: the column whose rate is drawn. Defaults to `None`, which
            uses the dataset's label, or else `_DEFAULT_RATE`.
        court_name: the column with courtpy's name for each case's court.
            Defaults to "court_name".
        court_num: the column with courtpy's number for each case's
            court. Defaults to "court_num".
        jurisdiction: the folder of the jurisdiction's table of courts.
            Defaults to "federal".
        **kwargs: not used.

    """
    data = item.data
    column = _rate_column(item, column)
    table = pd.DataFrame({
        'court': courts.court_labels(
            data, court_name = court_name, court_num = court_num,
            jurisdiction = jurisdiction),
        'value': _numbers(data[column])}).dropna()
    rates = table.groupby('court', observed = True)['value'].agg(
        ['mean', 'size'])
    shares = _is_share(table['value'])
    axes = figure.subplots()
    places = np.arange(len(rates))
    axes.barh(places, rates['mean'])
    axes.set_yticks(places, [str(c) for c in rates.index])
    axes.invert_yaxis()
    for place, (rate, count) in zip(
            places, rates.itertuples(index = False), strict = True):
        axes.annotate(
            f' {_amount(rate, shares)} (n = {count:,})', (rate, place),
            va = 'center', fontsize = 'small')
    overall = table['value'].mean()
    axes.axvline(
        overall, color = '0.35', linestyle = '--',
        label = f'All courts: {_amount(overall, shares)}')
    # Room to the right of the longest bar for its label.

def draw(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    source: str = 'compare_with_idb',
    columns: int = 3,
    **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Draws a confusion matrix for each variable.

    Args:
        item: the dataset, with the table of `compare_with_idb`.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        source: the name of the table in the dataset's `tables`. Defaults
            to "compare_with_idb".
        columns: the most panels in a row. Defaults to 3.
        **kwargs: not used.

    """
    table = _table(item, source)
    panels = _court_panels(figure, table.index, columns, share_y = False)
    labels = ['True', 'False']
    for name, axes in panels.items():
        row = table.loc[name]
        counts = np.array([
            [row['both_true'], row['data_only']],
            [row['idb_only'], row['both_false']]], dtype = float)
        total = counts.sum()
        shares = counts / total if total else counts
        axes.imshow(shares, cmap = 'Blues', vmin = 0, vmax = 1)
        for (down, across), count in np.ndenumerate(counts):
            share = shares[down, across]
            axes.text(
                across, down, f'{count:,.0f}\n{share:.0%}',
                ha = 'center', va = 'center', fontsize = 'small',
                color = 'white' if share > 0.6 else 'black')
        axes.set_xticks([0, 1], labels)
        axes.set_yticks([0, 1], labels)
        axes.set_xlabel('IDB', fontsize = 'small')
        axes.set_ylabel('Data', fontsize = 'small')
        axes.minorticks_off()
        kappa = row['kappa']
        title = _words(str(name))
        if pd.notna(kappa):
            title = f'{title} (κ = {kappa:.2f})'
        axes.set_title(title, fontsize = 'small')

def draw(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    source: str = 'compare_with_idb_missing',
    alpha: float = 0.05,
    **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Draws the differences of each variable in each group.

    Args:
        item: the dataset, with the second table of `compare_with_idb`.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        source: the name of the table in the dataset's `tables`. Defaults
            to "compare_with_idb_missing".
        alpha: the p value below which a difference is starred. Defaults
            to 0.05.
        **kwargs: not used.

    """
    table = _table(item, source)
    groups = list(dict.fromkeys(table['group']))
    names = list(dict.fromkeys(table['variable']))
    differences = table.pivot_table(
        index = 'group', columns = 'variable', values = 'difference',
        aggfunc = 'first', dropna = False).reindex(
            index = groups, columns = names)
    p_values = table.pivot_table(
        index = 'group', columns = 'variable', values = 'p_value',
        aggfunc = 'first', dropna = False).reindex(
            index = groups, columns = names)
    coverage = table.drop_duplicates('group').set_index('group')[
        'coverage'].reindex(groups)
    points = differences.to_numpy(dtype = float) * 100
    significance = p_values.to_numpy(dtype = float)
    largest = np.nanmax(np.abs(points)) if np.isfinite(points).any() else 1
    axes = figure.subplots()
    image = axes.imshow(
        points, cmap = 'RdBu_r', vmin = -largest, vmax = largest,
        aspect = 'auto')
    for (down, across), value in np.ndenumerate(points):
        if np.isnan(value):
            continue
        starred = significance[down, across] < float(alpha)
        axes.text(
            across, down, f'{value:+.0f}' + ('*' if starred else ''),
            ha = 'center', va = 'center', fontsize = 'small',
            color = 'white' if abs(value) > 0.6 * largest else 'black')
    axes.set_xticks(
        range(len(names)), [_words(str(n)) for n in names],
        rotation = 45, ha = 'right')
    axes.set_yticks(range(len(groups)), [
        f'{group} ({share:.0%} in data)' if pd.notna(share)
        else str(group)
        for group, share in coverage.items()])
    axes.minorticks_off()
    colorbar = figure.colorbar(image, ax = axes)
    colorbar.set_label(
        'Share in data minus share missing (points)', fontsize = 'small')
    axes.set_title(
        f'* p < {float(alpha):g}', fontsize = 'small', loc = 'right')

def draw(

    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    issues: Sequence[str] | str = (),
    year: str = 'year',
    court_name: str = 'court_name',
    court_num: str = 'court_num',
    jurisdiction: str = 'federal',

    """Draws the number of cases with each issue in each court and year.

    Args:
        item: the cases.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        issues: the columns of flags to count, as a list or a
            comma-separated `str`. Required.
        year: the column with each case's year. Defaults to "year".
        court_name: the column with courtpy's name for each case's court.
            Defaults to "court_name".
        court_num: the column with courtpy's number for each case's

        columns: the most panels in a row. Defaults to 4.

        KeyError: if an issue is not a column of the cases.

    named = utilities.listify(issues)
    if not named:
        message = 'issues_over_time needs "issues": columns of flags'
        raise ValueError(message)
    cases.require_columns(data, named, 'issues_over_time')

            data, cases.column_as_flags(data, issue).astype('int64'),
            year = year, court_name = court_name, court_num = court_num,
            jurisdiction = jurisdiction, how = 'sum')
        for issue in named}

    panels = _court_panels(figure, every, columns)

                label = _words(issue))

    figure.legend(
        handles, labels, loc = 'outside upper center',
        ncols = min(len(named), 4))

    figure.supylabel('Cases')

def draw(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    dissents: bool = False,
    minimum: int = 1,
    labels: bool = True,
    judge: str = 'judge',
    case: str = 'case_id',
    party: str = 'judge_party',
    dissented: str = 'judge_dissented',
    seed: int = 0,
    **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Draws the network of the judges.

    Args:
        item: the votes (see `cases_to_votes`), a row for each judge on
            each case.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        dissents: whether to join judges by the dissents of one from the
            other, instead of by the cases they decided together.
            Defaults to `False`.
        minimum: the fewest cases that join two judges to draw the line
            between them. Defaults to 1.
        labels: whether to write each judge's name. Defaults to `True`.
        judge: the column with each judge's name. Defaults to "judge".
        case: the column with each vote's case. Defaults to "case_id".
        party: the column with the party of the president who appointed
            the judge (-1 or 1). Defaults to "judge_party".
        dissented: the column of flags of whether the judge dissented,
            for `dissents`. Defaults to "judge_dissented".
        seed: the seed of the layout, so that the same data is drawn the
            same way. Defaults to 0.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if the votes lack a column that is needed.

    """
    networkx = amos.utilities.import_tool('networkx')
    data = item.data
    needed = [judge, case, *([dissented] if dissents else [])]
    cases.require_columns(
        data, needed, 'judge_network (make votes with cases_to_votes)')
    pairs = _pairs(data, judge, case, dissented if dissents else None)
    pairs = pairs[pairs['cases'] >= minimum]
    graph = networkx.Graph()
    graph.add_nodes_from(data[judge].dropna().astype(str).unique())
    graph.add_weighted_edges_from(
        pairs[['first', 'second', 'cases']].itertuples(index = False))
    parties = (
        pd.to_numeric(data[party], errors = 'coerce').groupby(
            data[judge].astype(str)).first()
        if party in data.columns else pd.Series(dtype = float))
    colors = [
        _PARTY_COLORS.get(int(parties[n]), '0.6')
        if n in parties.index and not pd.isna(parties[n]) else '0.6'
        for n in graph.nodes]
    weights = np.array(
        [graph.edges[e]['weight'] for e in graph.edges], dtype = float)
    widths = 0.5 + 3.5 * weights / weights.max() if len(weights) else []
    axes = figure.subplots()
    layout = networkx.spring_layout(graph, seed = seed, weight = 'weight')
    networkx.draw_networkx_edges(
        graph, layout, ax = axes, width = widths, edge_color = '0.6',
        alpha = 0.7)
    networkx.draw_networkx_nodes(
        graph, layout, ax = axes, node_color = colors, node_size = 120)
    if labels:
        networkx.draw_networkx_labels(
            graph, layout, ax = axes, font_size = 6)
    axes.set_axis_off()

def draw(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    column: str | None = None,
    minimum: int = 1,
    court_name: str = 'court_name',
    court_num: str = 'court_num',
    lower_court_name: str = 'lower_court_name',
    lower_court_num: str = 'lower_court_num',
    jurisdiction: str = 'federal',
    **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Draws the rate of `column` for each court below.

    Args:
        item: the cases.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        column: the column whose rate is drawn. Defaults to `None`, which
            uses the dataset's label, or else `_DEFAULT_RATE`.
        minimum: the fewest cases of a court below to draw it. Defaults
            to 1.
        court_name: the column with courtpy's name for each case's court.
            Defaults to "court_name".
        court_num: the column with courtpy's number for each case's
            court. Defaults to "court_num".
        lower_court_name: the column with courtpy's name for the court
            below. Defaults to "lower_court_name".
        lower_court_num: the column with courtpy's number for the court
            below. Defaults to "lower_court_num".
        jurisdiction: the folder of the jurisdiction's table of courts.
            Defaults to "federal".
        **kwargs: not used.

    """
    data = item.data
    column = _rate_column(item, column)
    table = pd.DataFrame({
        'court': courts.court_labels(
            data, court_name = court_name, court_num = court_num,
            jurisdiction = jurisdiction),
        'lower': courts.court_labels(
            data, court_name = lower_court_name,
            court_num = lower_court_num, jurisdiction = jurisdiction),
        'value': _numbers(data[column])}).dropna()
    shares = _is_share(table['value'])
    rates = table.groupby(['court', 'lower'], observed = True)[
        'value'].agg(['mean', 'size'])
    rates = rates[rates['size'] >= minimum]
    axes = figure.subplots()
    places = np.arange(len(rates))
    reviewing = rates.index.get_level_values('court')
    for number, court in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(reviewing)):

        axes.barh(
            places[rows], rates['mean'].to_numpy()[rows],
            color = f'C{number % 10}', label = str(court))
    lowers = rates.index.get_level_values('lower')
    axes.set_yticks(
        places,
        [f'{lower} ({int(n):,})'
         for lower, n in zip(lowers, rates['size'], strict = True)],
        fontsize = 'x-small')
    axes.invert_yaxis()
    axes.set_xlabel(_rate_name(column, shares))
    _as_percent(axes.xaxis, shares)
    figure.legend(
        title = 'Reviewing court', loc = 'outside lower center',
        ncols = 3, fontsize = 'small')

def draw(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    figure: Any,
    *,
    column: str | None = None,
    by: str | None = None,
    size: int = 3,
    **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Draws the rate of `column` for each composition of the panel.

    Args:
        item: the cases, with the parties of their judges.
        figure: the figure to draw on.
        column: the column whose rate is drawn. Defaults to `None`, which
            uses the dataset's label, or else `_DEFAULT_RATE`.
        by: a column to split the cases by. A column of flags splits them
            into those with the flag and the others. Defaults to `None`.
        size: the number of judges on the panels to draw. Defaults to 3.
        **kwargs: not used.

    """
    data = item.data
    column = _rate_column(item, column)
    table = pd.DataFrame({
        'composition': judges.panel_compositions(data, size),
        'value': _numbers(data[column]),
        'group': _groups(data, by)}).dropna()
    rates = table.groupby(
        ['group', 'composition'], observed = False)['value'].agg(
            ['mean', 'size'])
    groups = list(dict.fromkeys(rates.index.get_level_values('group')))
    names = list(table['composition'].cat.categories)
    axes = figure.subplots()
    width = 0.8 / len(groups)
    for place, group in enumerate(groups):
        found = rates.loc[group].reindex(names)
        spots = np.arange(len(names)) + (place - (len(groups) - 1) / 2) * (
            width)
        bars = axes.bar(
            spots, found['mean'].fillna(0).to_numpy(), width,
            label = group if by else None)
        for bar, count in zip(
                bars, found['size'].fillna(0), strict = True):
            if count:
                axes.annotate(
                    f'n = {int(count):,}',
                    (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height()),
                    ha = 'center', va = 'bottom', fontsize = 'x-small')
    shares = _is_share(table['value'])
    axes.set_xticks(np.arange(len(names)), names)
    axes.set_xlabel('Panel (D: Democratic appointee, R: Republican)')
    axes.set_ylabel(_rate_name(column, shares))
    _as_percent(axes.yaxis, shares)
    if by:
        axes.legend(title = _words(by))

            court. Defaults to "court_num".
        jurisdiction: the folder of the jurisdiction's table of courts.
            Defaults to "federal".
        columns: the most panels in a row. Defaults to 4.
        **kwargs: not used.

    """
    data = item.data
    column = _rate_column(item, column)
    rates = _yearly(
        data, _numbers(data[column]), year = year,
        court_name = court_name, court_num = court_num,
        jurisdiction = jurisdiction, how = 'mean')
    shares = _is_share(_numbers(data[column]))
    years = rates.columns.to_numpy(dtype = float)
    terms = _terms(years.min(), years.max() + 1)
    panels = _court_panels(figure, rates.index, columns)
    patch = amos.utilities.import_tool('matplotlib.patches').Patch
    for court, axes in panels.items():
        for start, end, party in terms:
            axes.axvspan(
                start, end, color = _PARTY_COLORS[party], alpha = 0.12,
                linewidth = 0)
        axes.plot(
            years, rates.loc[court].to_numpy(), color = '0.15',
            marker = '.')
        _as_percent(axes.yaxis, shares)
    figure.legend(
        handles = [
            patch(color = _PARTY_COLORS[-1], alpha = 0.3,
                  label = 'Democratic president'),
            patch(color = _PARTY_COLORS[1], alpha = 0.3,
                  label = 'Republican president')],
        loc = 'outside upper center', ncols = 2)
    figure.supxlabel('Year')
    figure.supylabel(_rate_name(column, shares))

def column_as_flags(data: pd.DataFrame, column: str) -> pd.Series:
    """Returns a column of a table of cases as plain booleans.

    Flags combined with `&` and `|` need plain booleans without missing
    values. A missing value (or a missing column) is false. Text (as in a
    table loaded from a CSV file) is true if it is "true", "t", "1", or "yes"
    (in any case).

    Args:
        data: the cases.
        column: name of the column.

    Returns:
        The column as plain booleans, or a column of false values if `data`
            has no such column.

    """
    if column not in data.columns:
        return pd.Series(False, index = data.index)
    values = data[column]
    # pandas reads text as the "str" type, or as `object` when it is mixed
    # with other values.
    if values.dtype == object or pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(values.dtype):
        values = values.map(
            lambda v: str(v).strip().lower() in _TRUE
            if isinstance(v, str) else bool(v) if pd.notna(v) else False)
    return values.astype('boolean').fillna(False).astype(bool)

def require_columns(
    data: pd.DataFrame,
    columns: Iterable[str],
    name: str,
    *,
    hint: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Raises an error if a table lacks columns.

    Args:
        data: the table.
        columns: names of the columns that are needed.
        name: what needs them (such as "a table of votes" or a technique's
            name), for the message.
        hint: a sentence added to the message, such as how to make the
            columns. Defaults to `None`.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if a column is missing. The message names the missing
            columns and `name`.

    """
    missing = [c for c in columns if c not in data.columns]
    if missing:
        message = f'{name} needs the columns {missing}, which are missing'
        if hint:
            message = f'{message}. {hint}'
        raise KeyError(message)

def select_whole_cases(
    data: pd.DataFrame,
    query: str | None,
    *,
    case_column: str = 'case_id') -> pd.Series:
    """Returns which rows a query selects, keeping each case whole.

    A table with several rows for each case (such as a row for each judge's
    vote) is selected a case at a time, so that a case is never split.

    Args:
        data: the table.
        query: an expression that `pandas.DataFrame.eval` reads (such as
            "year >= 2010 and not dissenting"), or `None`.
        case_column: the column with each row's case. Defaults to "case_id".

    Raises:
        KeyError: if `data` has no `case_column`.
        ValueError: if the query does not say whether each row is selected
            (such as "year + 1", which makes a number for each row).

    Returns:
        Whether each row is selected: every row without a query, and the
            rows of a case only if the query selects every one of them.

    """
    if not query:
        return pd.Series(True, index = data.index)
    require_columns(data, [case_column], 'select_whole_cases')
    message = (
        f'the query {query!r} must say whether each row is selected (true '
        f'or false), as "year >= 2010" does')
    found = data.eval(query)
    if not isinstance(found, pd.Series) or len(found) != len(data):
        raise ValueError(message)
    try:
        selected = column_as_flags(
            pd.DataFrame({'selected': found}, index = data.index),
            'selected')
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        raise ValueError(message) from error
    whole: pd.Series = selected.groupby(data[case_column]).transform('all')
    return whole

def split_cell(value: Any, separator: str = _SEPARATOR) -> list[Any]:
    """Returns the values in a cell of a table of cases, as a list.

    Rules that find several values (such as "panel_judges" or "agencies")
    join them with "; " so that the table can be saved as a CSV file.

    Args:
        value: a cell: text with `separator` between its values, a list (or
            tuple or array) of values, or a missing value.
        separator: the text between the values. Defaults to "; ".

    Returns:
        The values, with text trimmed of spaces and without blank values. A
            missing value or blank text has none.

    """
    if isinstance(value, list | tuple | np.ndarray):
        return [v for v in value if not isinstance(v, str) or v.strip()]
    if value is None or (not isinstance(value, str) and pd.isna(value)):
        return []
    pieces = (p.strip() for p in str(value).split(separator))
    return [p for p in pieces if p]

pandas stores a column of booleans with missing values (such as "published", which is unknown for some cases) as plain objects, and a column of whole numbers with missing values (such as "year") as decimals. Such columns become the "boolean" and "Int64" types, which allow missing values.

def tidy(data: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Gives columns of booleans or whole numbers with missing values a type.

    `pandas` stores a column of booleans with missing values (such as
    "published", which is unknown for some cases) as plain objects, and a
    column of whole numbers with missing values (such as "year") as decimals.
    Such columns become the "boolean" and "Int64" types, which allow missing
    values.

    Args:
        data: a table of cases.

    Returns:
        The table, with those columns changed.

    """
    for column in data.columns:
        values = data[column].dropna()
        if len(values) == 0:
            continue
        if data[column].dtype == object and values.map(
            lambda v: isinstance(v, bool)).all():
            data[column] = data[column].astype('boolean')
        elif (
            column in _WHOLE_NUMBERS
            and pd.api.types.is_float_dtype(data[column].dtype)
            and (values == values.round()).all()):
            data[column] = data[column].astype('Int64')
    return data

docs.title: datasets
docs.text:
The kinds of datasets that courtpy makes, one for each kind of row.

Each is an amos.Dataset, so every technique of amos works on it, and everything that amos says about datasets is true of it. What a class adds is what its rows are, the column that labels them, and how to save and load it. courtpy's loaders make Cases, and its shapers turn one kind into another:

Dataset One row for each Labeled by Made by Cases Case, with its information and the text of its sections. case_id courtpy's loaders, votes_to_cases, dockets_to_cases Dockets Docket number of each case, with the case's columns. A case that consolidated several appeals has a row for each. case_docket cases_to_dockets Votes Judge on each case (or each docket), with the case's columns and the judge's vote. vote_id cases_to_votes, dockets_to_votes Judges Judge, with what is known about the judge and summaries of the judge's votes. judge_nid cases_to_judges Courts Court, with summaries of its cases and their judges. court_num cases_to_courts CaseTypes Case type (such as "criminal" or "tort"), with summaries of its cases. case_type cases_to_case_types PartyTypes Party type, with summaries of the cases of parties of that type. party_type cases_to_party_types

Cases, Dockets, and Votes can be made from each other. Judges, Courts, CaseTypes, and PartyTypes summarize many cases, and they keep nothing about any one case (such as its docket number or date), so there is no going back from them.

save saves a dataset whole (with its label, split, history, and anything that techniques have added) in a joblib file, and its data as a table that a spreadsheet or another program can read, as the save_data technique of amos does. load loads either one:

import courtpy

cases = courtpy.Cases.load('cases.csv')
cases.save('cases.parquet')
Contents

CaseTypes: a table with one row for each case type. Cases: a table with one row for each case. CourtData: base class for courtpy's datasets. Courts: a table with one row for each court. Dockets: a table with one row for each docket number of each case. Judges: a table with one row for each judge. PartyTypes: a table with one row for each party type. Votes: a table with one row for each judge on each case. _TABLE_FORMATS: the format of the table that CourtData.save saves, by the extension of the file.

@classmethod
def adopt(cls, dataset: amos.Dataset) -> Self:
    """Returns `dataset` as a dataset of this kind.

    The new dataset shares everything with `dataset` (its data, label,
    split, history, and so on), so a shaper can hand on a dataset of
    another kind. If the data has a column named `key`, it labels the
    rows.

    Args:
        dataset: a dataset of any kind.

    Returns:
        `dataset` itself if it is already of this kind, and otherwise a
            new dataset of this kind with the same attributes.

    """
    if type(dataset) is cls:
        adopted = dataset
    else:
        adopted = cls.__new__(cls)
        adopted.__dict__.update(dataset.__dict__)
    adopted._label_rows()
    return adopted

@classmethod
def load(cls, path: pathlib.Path | str, **kwargs: Any) -> Self:
    """Loads a dataset that `save` saved, or a table of one.

    A joblib file holds the whole dataset, which goes on from where it
    was saved. A table (such as a CSV or parquet file) holds only its
    data: the column named `key` labels the rows again, and columns of
    booleans and whole numbers with missing values get the types that
    allow them (see `cases.tidy`).

    Args:
        path: the path of the file.
        **kwargs: arguments of `amos.Dataset.create`, such as "label"
            and "groups".

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if there is no file at `path`.
        TypeError: if the file holds a courtpy dataset of another kind.

    Returns:
        The dataset.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path).expanduser()
    if not path.is_file():
        message = f'there is no file of {cls.__name__} at {path}'
        raise FileNotFoundError(message)
    loaded = amos.Dataset.create(path, **kwargs)
    if isinstance(loaded, CourtData) and not isinstance(loaded, cls):
        message = (
            f'{path} holds {type(loaded).__name__}, not {cls.__name__}: '
            f'load it with courtpy.{type(loaded).__name__}.load'
        )
        raise TypeError(message)
    dataset = loaded if isinstance(loaded, cls) else cls.adopt(loaded)
    if not isinstance(loaded, CourtData):
        dataset.data = cases.tidy(dataset.data)
        dataset._label_rows()
    return dataset

def save(
    self,
    path: pathlib.Path | str,
    *,
    clerk: nagata.FileManager | None = None,
    compress: int | bool = 0) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Saves the whole dataset, and its data as a table.

    The `save_data` technique of `amos` saves the dataset in a joblib file
    named for `path` (such as "cases.joblib" beside "cases.csv"), which
    `load` loads as it was, and the data in `path`, in the format of its
    extension: ".csv", ".parquet", or ".xlsx". A path ending in ".joblib"
    (or with no extension) saves only the dataset. Several values in one
    cell (such as the lists that `split_values` makes) are saved as text,
    with "; " between them, as courtpy's rules write them. The dataset's
    history records where the files are.

    Args:
        path: the path of the table. Its folder is made if needed.
        clerk: the file manager that saves the files. Defaults to `None`,
            in which case one for the folder of `path` is used, so
            nothing else is made.
        compress: how much joblib compresses the file of the dataset,
            from 0 (not at all) to 9. Defaults to 0.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if the extension of `path` is not one listed above.

    Returns:
        The paths of the files that were saved.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix not in _TABLE_FORMATS:
        message = (
            f'{path.name} must end in one of '
            f'{[s for s in _TABLE_FORMATS if s]}')
        raise ValueError(message)
    folder = path.parent
    folder.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    if clerk is None:
        clerk = nagata.FileManager(
            root_folder = folder,
            input_folder = folder,
            interim_folder = folder,
            output_folder = folder)
    joined = copy.copy(self)
    joined.data = _join_lists(self.data)
    joined.history = list(self.history)
    amos.savers.SaveData(clerk = clerk).apply(
        joined,
        folder = folder,
        file_name = path.stem,
        table_format = _TABLE_FORMATS[suffix] or False,
        compress = compress)
    self.history.append(joined.history[-1])
    return [pathlib.Path(file) for file in joined.history[-1]['files']]

docs.title: options
docs.text:
Default settings for courtpy.

These are module-level constants so that a project built on courtpy can change them before they are used (for example, courtpy.options._MIN_INTERVAL = 2.0 to slow down requests to the CourtListener API). Tables of the federal courts and the presidents are in "instructions/federal" (see courtpy.courts and courtpy.politics).

Contents

_API_URL: base address of the CourtListener REST API (version 4). _BULK_PREFIX: folder of the CourtListener bulk data in its bucket. _BULK_URL: address of the public bucket with CourtListener's bulk data. _CHUNK_SIZE: number of saved cases given to a process at a time when parsing with several processes. _COURT_GROUPS: names for groups of CourtListener court ids. _DATA_SUBFOLDER: the folder of the amos workspace's data folder that holds courtpy's downloads. _DEFAULT_CODERS: techniques that code variables after cases are parsed. _DEFAULT_JURISDICTION: rulebooks used when none are named. _REQUIRED_RULEBOOKS: rulebooks applied to every case, after its source's header rulebook and before those that are named. _DOCKET_SKIPPED: fields of a CourtListener docket that are not kept with a saved case. _ENV_API_KEY: environment variable that can hold the API key. _ENV_CONFIG: environment variable that can name the configuration folder. _ENV_DATA: environment variable that can name the data folder. _IDB_CIRCUITS: the Federal Judicial Center's Integrated Database's code for the circuit of each CourtListener court of appeals. _IDB_FIRST_YEAR: the first year of the Integrated Database's records of appeals. _JUDGE_GRACE: years after a judge leaves a court in which an opinion may still name the judge. _KEYRING_SERVICE: name under which the API key is kept in a keyring. _KEYRING_USERNAME: user name under which the API key is kept. _LARGE_SECTIONS: sections of text that are not kept in a case table unless asked. _MAX_WAIT: most seconds to wait when the API asks for a pause. _MIN_INTERVAL: fewest seconds between requests to the API. _OPINION_FIELDS: opinion fields requested from the CourtListener API. _SCDB_FILES: the part of the name of each file of the Supreme Court Database that courtpy uses, by what courtpy.scdb calls each. _SCDB_LINK: the words of the links to those files on the page of a release of the Supreme Court Database. _SCDB_PAGE: address of the page that links to the releases of the Supreme Court Database. _SCDB_RELEASE: pattern for the address of the page of a release of the modern Supreme Court Database. _SOURCES: sources of court opinions that courtpy can read. _TEXT_FIELDS: CourtListener fields with the text of an opinion, in the order they are preferred. _TIMEOUT: seconds to wait for a response from a server. _USER_AGENT: how courtpy identifies itself to servers.

docs.title: secrets
docs.text:
Keeps the CourtListener API key secret, outside of projects and packages.

The key is never written in a project's settings or in courtpy itself, so it cannot be shared or committed by accident. Store it once, and courtpy finds it whenever it is needed:

import courtpy

courtpy.secrets.set_api_key("your-key")

or, from a terminal (which asks for the key without showing it):

courtpy key set

get_api_key looks for the key in these places, in order, and uses the first one it finds:

  1. The COURTLISTENER_API_KEY environment variable.
  2. The system keyring: Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain, or the Secret Service on Linux (if one is running).
  3. The secrets file in courtpy's configuration folder (see secrets_path), which is in the user's home folder, not in any project.
  4. A .env file in the current folder with a line such as COURTLISTENER_API_KEY=your-key. Keep such a file out of version control (courtpy's own .gitignore excludes it).
Contents

MissingAPIKeyError: raised when no API key can be found. delete_api_key: removes the stored API key. find_api_key: returns the API key and where it was found. get_api_key: returns the API key. mask: hides most of a key so that it can be shown. secrets_path: returns the path of the secrets file. set_api_key: stores the API key. logger: the module's logger, which reports problems with the keyring and the secrets file. _FILE_SECTION: the section of the secrets file that holds the key. _FILE_SETTING: the setting, in _FILE_SECTION, that holds the key. _STORES: the places that set_api_key can store the key ("auto", "keyring", or "file").

docs.text:
Removes the API key from the keyring and the secrets file.

A key in an environment variable or a .env file is not changed.

Descriptions of the places the key was removed from.

def delete_api_key() -> list[str]:
    """Removes the API key from the keyring and the secrets file.

    A key in an environment variable or a `.env` file is not changed.

    Returns:
        Descriptions of the places the key was removed from.

    """
    removed = []
    backend = _keyring()
    if backend is not None:
        try:
            if backend.get_password(*_keyring_names()) is not None:
                backend.delete_password(*_keyring_names())
                removed.append('the system keyring')
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            logger.debug('the keyring could not be changed: %s', error)
    path = secrets_path()
    contents = _read_file(path)
    if contents.get(_FILE_SECTION, {}).get(_FILE_SETTING):
        del contents[_FILE_SECTION][_FILE_SETTING]
        _write_file(path, contents)
        removed.append(str(path))
    return removed

def find_api_key() -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    """Returns the API key and a description of where it was found.

    Returns:
        The key and where it was found, or `None` if there is no key in any of
            the places that `get_api_key` looks.

    """
    value = os.environ.get(options._ENV_API_KEY, '').strip()
    if value:
        return value, f'the {options._ENV_API_KEY} environment variable'
    backend = _keyring()
    if backend is not None:
        try:
            value = (backend.get_password(*_keyring_names()) or '').strip()
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            logger.debug('the keyring could not be read: %s', error)
            value = ''
        if value:
            return value, 'the system keyring'
    path = secrets_path()
    value = str(
        _read_file(path).get(_FILE_SECTION, {}).get(_FILE_SETTING, '')).strip()
    if value:
        return value, str(path)
    dotenv = pathlib.Path.cwd() / '.env'
    value = _read_dotenv(dotenv).get(options._ENV_API_KEY, '').strip()
    if value:
        return value, str(dotenv)
    return None

def get_api_key(required: bool = True) -> str | None:
    """Returns the CourtListener API key.

    Args:
        required: whether to raise an error if there is no key. Defaults to
            `True`.

    Raises:
        MissingAPIKeyError: if there is no key and `required` is `True`.

    Returns:
        The key, or `None` if there is no key and `required` is `False`.

    """
    found = find_api_key()
    if found is None:
        if required:
            raise MissingAPIKeyError
        return None
    return found[0]

def mask(key: str) -> str:
    """Hides most of `key` so that it can be shown.

    Args:
        key: a secret.

    Returns:
        The first and last four characters of `key`, with dots between them,
            or only dots if `key` is short.

    """
    dot = chr(0x2022)
    if len(key) <= 12:
        return dot * len(key)
    return key[:4] + dot * 8 + key[-4:]

def set_api_key(key: str, *, store: str = 'auto') -> str:
    """Stores the CourtListener API key outside of any project.

    Args:
        key: the API key, from the "API" page of a CourtListener profile.
        store: "keyring" for the system keyring, "file" for the secrets file
            (see `secrets_path`), or "auto" (the default) for the keyring if
            one is available and the file otherwise.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: if `store` is "keyring" and the keyring cannot be used.
        ValueError: if `key` is blank or `store` is not one of those.

    Returns:
        A description of where the key was stored.

    """
    key = key.strip()
    if not key:
        message = 'the API key is blank'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if key.lower().startswith('token '):
        # People often copy the whole header value.
        key = key[6:].strip()
    if store not in _STORES:
        message = f'store must be one of {list(_STORES)}, not {store!r}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if store in ('auto', 'keyring'):
        backend = _keyring()
        try:
            if backend is None:
                message = 'no system keyring is available'
                raise RuntimeError(message)  # noqa: TRY301
            backend.set_password(*_keyring_names(), key)
        except Exception as error:
            if store == 'keyring':
                message = f'the key could not be stored in the keyring: {error}'
                raise RuntimeError(message) from error
            logger.info(
                'the keyring is not available (%s), so a file is used', error)
        else:
            return 'the system keyring'
    path = secrets_path()
    contents = _read_file(path)
    contents.setdefault(_FILE_SECTION, {})[_FILE_SETTING] = key
    _write_file(path, contents)
    return str(path)

docs.title: config_folder()
docs.text:
Returns the folder for courtpy's settings and secrets.

The folder is outside of any project or package, so that a secret (such as the CourtListener API key) is never saved in a project's files or shared with them. It is the folder named by the COURTPY_CONFIG_DIR environment variable, if it is set. Otherwise, it is "courtpy" in the user's application data folder on Windows ("%APPDATA%"), or in "~/.config" (or "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME") on other systems.

Returns:

Type Description Path

The path of the folder. It is not created.

Source code in src/courtpy/core/utilities.py 
def config_folder() -> pathlib.Path:
    """Returns the folder for courtpy's settings and secrets.

    The folder is outside of any project or package, so that a secret (such as
    the CourtListener API key) is never saved in a project's files or shared
    with them. It is the folder named by the `COURTPY_CONFIG_DIR` environment
    variable, if it is set. Otherwise, it is "courtpy" in the user's
    application data folder on Windows ("%APPDATA%"), or in
    "~/.config" (or "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME") on other systems.

    Returns:
        The path of the folder. It is not created.

    """
    named = os.environ.get(options._ENV_CONFIG)
    if named:
        return pathlib.Path(named).expanduser()
    if sys.platform == 'win32':
        base = (
            os.environ.get('APPDATA')
            or pathlib.Path.home() / 'AppData' / 'Roaming')
        return pathlib.Path(base) / 'courtpy'
    base = os.environ.get('XDG_CONFIG_HOME') or pathlib.Path.home() / '.config'
    return pathlib.Path(base) / 'courtpy'

def data_folder() -> pathlib.Path:
    """Returns the folder for large downloads, such as bulk data.

    Bulk data files are very large (the opinions alone are more than 50 GB),
    so they are kept outside of projects, where every project can share
    them. The folder is the one named by the `COURTPY_DATA_DIR` environment
    variable, if it is set. Otherwise, it is `options._DATA_SUBFOLDER`
    ("courts") in the data folder of the `amos` workspace, which is where
    every `amos` project keeps its data (see `amos.clerks.workspace`): with
    projects in "projects/code", it is "projects/data/courts".

    Returns:
        The path of the folder. It is not created.

    """
    named = os.environ.get(options._ENV_DATA)
    if named:
        return pathlib.Path(named).expanduser()
    return (
        amos.clerks.workspace() / amos.options._DATA_FOLDER
        / options._DATA_SUBFOLDER)

def expand_courts(courts: str | Iterable[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    """Turns court ids and names of groups of courts into court ids.

    Args:
        courts: CourtListener court ids (such as "ca1" or "scotus") or names of
            groups in `options._COURT_GROUPS` (such as "federal_appellate"),
            as a list or a comma-separated `str`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if no courts are named.

    Returns:
        The court ids, in order, without repeats.

    """
    found: list[str] = []
    for name in listify(courts):
        for court in options._COURT_GROUPS.get(name.lower(), (name.lower(),)):
            if court not in found:
                found.append(court)
    if not found:
        message = 'name at least one court (such as "ca1") or group of courts'
        raise ValueError(message)
    return found

def listify(item: Any) -> list[str]:
    """Returns a setting as a list of names.

    Args:
        item: `None`, a `str` (which may list names separated by commas), or an
            iterable of names.

    Returns:
        The names, with surrounding spaces removed and blank names dropped.

    """
    if item is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(item, str):
        item = item.split(',')
    elif not isinstance(item, Iterable):
        item = [item]
    return [str(name).strip() for name in item if str(name).strip()]

def locate(path: pathlib.Path | str, clerk: Any = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Returns a file named in settings, found as a clerk finds files.

    Args:
        path: a path, which may begin with "~" for the user's home folder.
        clerk: the file manager of a project (a `nagata.FileManager`).
            Defaults to `None`.

    Returns:
        `path` itself if it is absolute, exists in the current folder, or
            there is no `clerk`, and otherwise `path` in the clerk's input
            folder.

    """
    resolved = pathlib.Path(str(path)).expanduser()
    if clerk is None or resolved.is_absolute() or resolved.exists():
        return resolved
    return pathlib.Path(clerk.input_folder) / resolved

def parse_date(text: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Returns the first date in `text` as an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

    Args:
        text: text with a date written out (such as "March 3, 2010" or
            "Mar. 3, 2010") or in ISO format ("2010-03-03").

    Returns:
        The date, or `None` if there is no valid date in `text`.

    """
    if not text:
        return None
    match = _ISO_DATE.search(text)
    if match:
        year, month, day = (int(part) for part in match.groups())
    else:
        match = _WRITTEN_DATE.search(text)
        if match is None:
            return None
        month = _MONTHS[match.group(1).upper()[:3]]
        day, year = int(match.group(2)), int(match.group(3))
    try:
        return datetime.date(year, month, day).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        return None

def read_csv(path: pathlib.Path | str, **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Loads a CSV file that is in UTF-8 or Windows-1252.

    The files of other researchers' data are not all in UTF-8, and some have
    been in one encoding in one year and another in the next.

    Args:
        path: the path of the file, which may begin with "~" for the user's
            home folder. A zip archive of one CSV file is read as that file.
        **kwargs: arguments for `pandas.read_csv`.

    Returns:
        The table.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path).expanduser()
    table: pd.DataFrame
    try:
        table = pd.read_csv(path, encoding = 'utf-8-sig', **kwargs)
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        table = pd.read_csv(path, encoding = 'cp1252', **kwargs)
    return table

def to_bool(value: Any) -> bool:
    """Converts a setting or a CSV cell to a boolean.

    Args:
        value: a `bool`, a number, or text such as "TRUE", "yes", "1", "t",
            "FALSE", "no", "0", or "f" (in any case). Blank text is `False`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if `value` is text that is not one of those.

    Returns:
        The boolean value.

    """
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return value
    if value is None:
        return False
    if isinstance(value, int | float):
        return bool(value)
    text = str(value).strip().lower()
    if text in {'true', 't', 'yes', 'y', '1'}:
        return True
    if text in {'false', 'f', 'no', 'n', '0', ''}:
        return False
    message = f'{value!r} is not TRUE or FALSE'
    raise ValueError(message)

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
The techniques of the "critic" stage, which check and evaluate court data.

Its modules, audits (the evaluators that check the data) and inferers (the effects of panels), can also be imported from courtpy itself (courtpy.audits and courtpy.inferers), which is where their techniques are documented.

docs.title: audits
docs.text:
Techniques that check court data and how well it was coded.

Each is an amos evaluator (amos.evaluators.Evaluator), so it is added to the amos library when courtpy is imported, can be named in the settings of a "critic" worker, and adds a table to the dataset's tables under its name. Unlike amos's audits, they check the data, not a fitted model, so they need no model.

Technique Checks Needs audit_random_assignment Whether the traits of cases (such as their types, and whether they review an agency) are balanced across the compositions of their panels within each court in each year, as random assignment of panels would make them. Cases, with the judges' parties (from add_biography or code_panels). audit_parsing How many cases lack what the rules should find (the court, the court below, the judges, the year, or the outcome), have panels of another size, or have a header's disposition that disagrees with the decision that the opinion states, with examples to read. Cases. audit_coverage How many cases of each court in each year the data has, against the appeals that the Federal Judicial Center's Integrated Database records, and so how much of each court's work it covers. Cases of the courts of appeals, with "year". validate_coding How often courtpy's coding agrees with another source's (such as the Integrated Database after add_idb, or the Supreme Court Database after add_scdb): the share of cases on which they agree and Cohen's kappa. Cases, with both columns of each pair. Contents

AuditCoverage: compares the cases of each court in each year with the appeals of the Integrated Database. AuditParsing: counts the cases that lack what the rules should find, or whose parts disagree. AuditRandomAssignment: checks that the traits of cases are balanced across the compositions of their panels. ValidateCoding: measures how often courtpy's coding agrees with another source's. _BALANCE_TRAITS: the traits of cases checked for balance when none are named. _RULINGS: the rulings that a header's disposition and an opinion's decision are compared on. _VALIDATION_CODES: the codes that mean true in the other source's columns that have codes, unless others are named. _VALIDATIONS: the pairs of columns compared when none are named, if the data has them.

Bases: Evaluator

Compares the cases of each court in each year with the database's.

The Federal Judicial Center's Integrated Database records every appeal that the courts of appeals decide. For each court and year of the cases, the table has how many cases the data has, how many appeals the database records as decided (by the year of their judgment), and the share of them that the data has, which shows which courts and years a study's cases (such as CourtListener's) leave out. If both have publication, it has the same for published opinions.

The database's records come from fjc-idb (see courtpy.fjc_idb.appeals), or from "source".

def evaluate(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    *,
    source: Any = None,
    folder: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    download: bool = True,
    year: str = 'year',
    court_name: str = 'court_name',
    court_num: str = 'court_num',
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns the coverage of each court in each year.

    Args:
        item: the cases of the courts of appeals.
        source: the database's table of appeals, or the path of a file
            of it (see `courtpy.fjc_idb.AddIdb`). Defaults to `None`, in
            which case the database's records of the years of the cases
            are read (and downloaded, if `download`).
        folder: the folder of the database's yearly files, without a
            `source`. Defaults to `None`, for fjc-idb's folder in
            courtpy's data folder.
        download: whether to download the yearly files that are missing,
            without a `source`. Defaults to `True`.
        year: the column with each case's year. Defaults to "year".
        court_name: the column with courtpy's name for each case's court.
            Defaults to "court_name".
        court_num: the column with courtpy's number for each case's
            court. Defaults to "court_num".
        **kwargs: not used.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if the cases have no `year`, or the database's table
            has no "circuit" or "judgment_date".

    Returns:
        A row for each court (by its label) and year, with "cases",
            "idb_appeals", and "coverage" (and "published",
            "idb_published", and "published_coverage" if both have
            publication).

    """
    data = item.data
    cases.require_columns(data, [year], 'audit_coverage')
    years = pd.to_numeric(data[year], errors = 'coerce')
    found = pd.DataFrame({
        'court': courts.court_labels(
            data, court_name = court_name, court_num = court_num),
        'year': years}).dropna()
    if found.empty:
        message = 'no case has a known court and year'
        raise ValueError(message)
    appeals = self._appeals(
        source, int(found['year'].min()), int(found['year'].max()) + 1,
        folder, download)
    cases.require_columns(
        appeals, ['circuit', 'judgment_date'], 'the database of appeals')
    recorded = pd.DataFrame({
        'court': appeals['circuit'].astype('string'),
        'year': pd.to_datetime(
            appeals['judgment_date'], errors = 'coerce').dt.year})
    group = ['court', 'year']
    counts = found.assign(court = found['court'].astype('string')).groupby(
        group).size().rename('cases')
    expected = recorded.dropna().groupby(group).size().rename(
        'idb_appeals')
    table = pd.concat([counts, expected], axis = 1).loc[counts.index]
    table['idb_appeals'] = table['idb_appeals'].fillna(0).astype('int64')
    table['coverage'] = table['cases'] / table['idb_appeals'].where(
        table['idb_appeals'] > 0)
    if 'published' in data.columns and 'published' in appeals.columns:
        mine = found.assign(
            court = found['court'].astype('string'),
            published = cases.column_as_flags(data, 'published')[
                found.index])
        theirs = recorded.assign(published = pd.to_numeric(
            appeals['published'], errors = 'coerce').fillna(0) > 0)
        table['published'] = mine.groupby(group)['published'].sum()
        table['idb_published'] = theirs.dropna().groupby(group)[
            'published'].sum().reindex(table.index).fillna(0).astype(
                'int64')
        table['published_coverage'] = table['published'] / table[
            'idb_published'].where(table['idb_published'] > 0)
    order = {c: n for n, c in enumerate(
        courts.court_labels(data).cat.categories)}
    return table.sort_index(
        key = lambda level: level.map(order) if level.name == 'court'
        else level)

Counts the cases that lack what the rules should find.

Each row is a check that the cases have: their court ("court_num"), the court below ("lower_court_num", except for a review of an agency or of the Board of Immigration Appeals), their judges ("panel_judges"), a panel of size judges ("panel_size"), their year, and their outcome ("outcome_reversal"), and that the disposition in the header ("disposition_...") agrees with the decision that the opinion states ("decision_...") where both are found. def evaluate(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    *,
    size: int = 3,
    examples: int = 10,
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns how many cases fail each check.

    Args:
        item: the cases.
        size: the number of judges that a panel should have. Defaults to
            3.
        examples: the most cases to list for each check. Defaults to 10.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Returns:
        A row for each check, labeled by it, with "cases" (how many fail
            it), "share" (of all the cases), and "examples" (the labels
            of the first that fail it, separated by "; ").

    """
    data = item.data
    checks: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
    if 'court_num' in data.columns:
        checks['no court'] = data['court_num'].isna()
    if 'lower_court_num' in data.columns:
        agency = pd.Series(False, index = data.index)
        for column in ('review_agency', 'review_immigration'):
            if column in data.columns:
                agency |= cases.column_as_flags(data, column)
        checks['no court below'] = data['lower_court_num'].isna() & ~agency
    if 'panel_judges' in data.columns:
        checks['no judges'] = ~_has_text(data['panel_judges'])
    if 'panel_size' in data.columns:
        checks[f'panel not of {size}'] = pd.to_numeric(
            data['panel_size'], errors = 'coerce') != size
    if 'year' in data.columns:
        checks['no year'] = data['year'].isna()
    if 'outcome_reversal' in data.columns:
        checks['no outcome'] = data['outcome_reversal'].isna()
    disagreement = _disagreement(data)
    if disagreement is not None:
        checks['disposition and decision disagree'] = disagreement
    total = max(len(data), 1)
    rows = []
    for check in checks.values():
        failing = check.fillna(False).astype(bool)
        rows.append({
            'cases': int(failing.sum()),
            'share': failing.sum() / total,
            'examples': cases._SEPARATOR.join(
                str(label) for label in data.index[failing][:examples])})
    return pd.DataFrame(
        rows, index = pd.Index(list(checks), name = 'check'))

Bases: Evaluator

Checks that the traits of cases are balanced across their panels.

Studies of panels (such as of whether a judge votes differently beside judges appointed by the other party) rely on panels being assigned to cases at random within a court. If they are, a trait of a case that the panel cannot change (such as whether it is criminal) has nothing to do with the panel's composition within each court in each year.

For each trait, the table has its mean for each composition of the panel ("DDD" to "RRR"; see courtpy.judges.panel_compositions), the correlation between the trait and the number of Republican appointees within each court and year (each stratum's mean removed), and the share of n_permutations random reassignments of the compositions within each court and year whose correlation is at least as far from 0 (a permutation test, with no assumption about how the trait is distributed). A trait is balanced if that share is at least alpha.

def evaluate(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    *,
    traits: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    size: int = 3,
    strata: Sequence[str] | str = ('court_num', 'year'),
    n_permutations: int = 1000,
    alpha: float = 0.05,
    seed: int = 0,
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns the balance of each trait across panel compositions.

    Args:
        item: the cases, with the parties of their judges.
        traits: the columns of the traits to check. Defaults to `None`,
            which checks those of `_BALANCE_TRAITS` that the cases have.
        size: the number of judges on the panels to check. Defaults to 3.
        strata: the columns within whose values panels are assigned.
            Defaults to "court_num" and "year".
        n_permutations: the number of random reassignments. Defaults to
            1000.
        alpha: the smallest share of reassignments at which a trait is
            balanced. Defaults to 0.05.
        seed: the seed of the random reassignments. Defaults to 0.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if no trait is named or found, or no case has a panel
            of `size` judges whose parties are known.

    Returns:
        A row for each trait, labeled by it, with the trait's mean for
            each composition, "correlation", "p_value", "balanced", and
            "cases" (the number of cases compared).

    """
    data = item.data
    named = utilities.listify(traits) or [
        t for t in _BALANCE_TRAITS if t in data.columns]
    if not named:
        message = 'audit_random_assignment needs "traits" to check'
        raise ValueError(message)
    cases.require_columns(data, named, 'audit_random_assignment')
    compositions = judges.panel_compositions(data, size)
    republicans = judges.republican_appointees(data, size)
    codes = _strata.stratum_codes(data, utilities.listify(strata))
    usable = republicans.notna() & (codes >= 0)
    if not usable.any():
        message = (
            f'no case has a panel of {size} judges whose parties are '
            f'known')
        raise ValueError(message)
    generator = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    rows = []
    for trait in named:
        values = _flags_or_numbers(data[trait])
        kept = (usable & values.notna()).to_numpy()
        found = values[kept].to_numpy(dtype = float)
        count = republicans[kept].to_numpy(dtype = float)
        stratum = pd.factorize(codes[kept])[0]
        centered = _strata.demean(found, stratum)
        counted = _strata.demean(count, stratum)
        observed = _correlation(centered, counted)
        # Shuffling within strata keeps each stratum's mean, so the
        # shuffled counts are already centered.
        extreme = sum(
            abs(_correlation(centered, _strata.permute_within(
                counted, stratum, generator))) >= abs(observed) - 1e-12
            for _ in range(n_permutations))
        p_value = (extreme + 1) / (n_permutations + 1)
        means = values[kept].groupby(
            compositions[kept], observed = False).mean()
        rows.append({
            **means.to_dict(),
            'correlation': observed,
            'p_value': p_value,
            'balanced': p_value >= alpha,
            'cases': int(kept.sum())})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, index = pd.Index(named, name = 'trait'))

Bases: Evaluator

Measures how often courtpy's coding agrees with another source's.

Each pair names a column of courtpy's (such as "published") and the other source's column for the same thing (such as "idb_published", after add_idb). Both are read as flags: true, nonzero, or (for the other source's column) one of its true_values. Only the cases with both are compared. Cohen's kappa is the agreement beyond what the shares of true values in each would give by chance (1 is perfect agreement, and 0 is no better than chance).

def evaluate(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    *,
    pairs: Mapping[str, str] | str | None = None,
    true_values: Mapping[str, Sequence[Any] | str] | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns the agreement of each pair of columns.

    Args:
        item: the cases.
        pairs: courtpy's columns and the other source's, as a `dict` or
            text such as "published = idb_published, type_criminal =
            idb_appeal_type". Defaults to `None`, which compares the
            pairs of `_VALIDATIONS` that the cases have.
        true_values: for a column of the other source with codes, the
            codes that mean true (as a list, or text separated by "|"),
            by the column's name. Defaults to `None`, which uses
            `_VALIDATION_CODES` for the columns it names.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if no pair is named or found.
        KeyError: if a column of a pair is not in the cases.

    Returns:
        A row for each pair, labeled by courtpy's column, with
            "reference" (the other column), "cases" (how many have both),
            "agreement", "kappa", "both_true", "both_false",
            "courtpy_only" (true only in courtpy's), and "reference_only".

    """
    data = item.data
    chosen = _parse_pairs(pairs) or {
        mine: theirs for mine, theirs in _VALIDATIONS.items()
        if mine in data.columns and theirs in data.columns}
    if not chosen:
        message = (
            'validate_coding needs "pairs" of columns to compare, such as '
            '"published = idb_published"')
        raise ValueError(message)
    cases.require_columns(
        data, [*chosen, *chosen.values()], 'validate_coding')
    codes = {
        column: [str(v) for v in utilities.listify(
            values.split('|') if isinstance(values, str) else values)]
        for column, values in {
            **_VALIDATION_CODES, **(true_values or {})}.items()}
    rows = []
    for mine, theirs in chosen.items():
        ours = _flags_or_numbers(data[mine]).ne(0).where(
            data[mine].notna())
        reference = data[theirs]
        if theirs in codes:
            truth = reference.astype('string').isin(codes[theirs])
        else:
            truth = _flags_or_numbers(reference).ne(0)
        truth = truth.where(reference.notna())
        both = ours.notna() & truth.notna()
        a = ours[both].astype(bool).to_numpy()
        b = truth[both].astype(bool).to_numpy()
        rows.append({
            'reference': theirs,
            'cases': int(both.sum()),
            **_agreement(a, b)})
    return pd.DataFrame(
        rows, index = pd.Index(list(chosen), name = 'column'))

docs.title: inferers
docs.text:
Techniques that infer the effects of panels on judges' votes.

panel_effects (PanelEffects) is an amos inferer (amos.inferers.Inferer), so it is added to the amos library when courtpy is imported, can be named in the settings of a "critic" worker, adds its table of effects to the dataset's tables under its name, and draws it as a coefficient_plot with "visualize".

Contents

PanelEffects: estimates the effect of a judge's colleagues on the judge's vote, with a test that reassigns panels at random. _Z_95: the number of standard errors on each side of an estimate in its 95% confidence interval.

docs.title: PanelEffects(contents=None, name='', parameters=dict()) dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: Inferer

Estimates the effect of a judge's colleagues on the judge's vote.

The data is Votes (see cases_to_votes): a row for each judge on each case, with the judge's vote (such as "vote_reversal"), the party of the president who appointed the judge ("judge_party", -1 or 1), and the mean party of the judge's colleagues on the panel ("colleagues_party"). The vote is regressed on the colleagues' party, the judge's own party, and (with "interact") their product, which says whether a judge of one party is moved more by the other party's colleagues, with a fixed effect for each court in each year, so that each vote is compared only with the votes of its own court and year (a linear probability model for a vote of yes or no).

Panels are assigned at random within a court (or so the design assumes; see audit_random_assignment), so the effects are causal if that holds. Two tests say how sure the estimates are:

  • The standard errors are clustered by case, since the judges of a case vote together, with Stata's correction for few clusters, and give the p-values and 95% confidence intervals.
  • A randomization test reassigns each vote's colleagues' party at random among the votes of the same court and year n_permutations times, and its p-value is the share of reassignments whose estimate is at least as far from 0 as the one found. It assumes nothing about the distribution of the votes.

The table has a row for each term, with "coefficient", "std_error", "t_statistic", "p_value", "ri_p_value" (for the colleagues' party and its product with the judge's party), "ci_lower", and "ci_upper".

def infer(
    self,
    item: amos.Dataset,
    *,
    outcome: str | None = None,
    treatment: str = 'colleagues_party',
    controls: Sequence[str] | str = ('judge_party',),
    interact: bool = True,
    strata: Sequence[str] | str = ('court_num', 'year'),
    cluster: str = 'case_id',
    n_permutations: int = 1000,
    seed: int = 0,
    **kwargs: Any) -> amos.inferers.Inference:
    """Returns the effects of the colleagues on the votes of `item`.

    Args:
        item: the votes, a row for each judge on each case.
        outcome: the column with each judge's vote. Defaults to `None`,
            which uses the dataset's label, or else "vote_reversal".
        treatment: the column with the judge's colleagues' party.
            Defaults to "colleagues_party".
        controls: other columns of the regression, as a list or a
            comma-separated `str`. Defaults to "judge_party".
        interact: whether to add the product of the treatment and the
            first control. Defaults to `True`.
        strata: the columns within whose values votes are compared (a
            fixed effect for each combination). Defaults to "court_num"
            and "year".
        cluster: the column whose values group the votes for the
            standard errors. Defaults to "case_id".
        n_permutations: the number of random reassignments of the
            treatment. 0 skips the randomization test. Defaults to 1000.
        seed: the seed of the random reassignments. Defaults to 0.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if the votes lack a column that is needed.
        ValueError: if no vote has every column.

    Returns:
        The table of effects, the arrays of the fitted regression, and
            the details to record.

    """
    data = item.data
    outcome = outcome or item.label or 'vote_reversal'
    named = utilities.listify(controls)
    grouped = utilities.listify(strata)
    cases.require_columns(
        data, [outcome, treatment, *named, *grouped, cluster],
        'panel_effects')
    numbers = pd.DataFrame({
        c: _numbers(data[c]) for c in [outcome, treatment, *named]})
    codes = _strata.stratum_codes(data, grouped)
    kept = (
        numbers.notna().all(axis = 1) & (codes >= 0)
        & data[cluster].notna()).to_numpy()
    if not kept.any():
        message = 'no vote has every column that panel_effects needs'
        raise ValueError(message)
    y = numbers.loc[kept, outcome].to_numpy(dtype = float)
    dose = numbers.loc[kept, treatment].to_numpy(dtype = float)
    others = numbers.loc[kept, named].to_numpy(dtype = float)
    stratum = pd.factorize(codes[kept])[0]
    groups = pd.factorize(data.loc[kept, cluster])[0]
    terms = [treatment]
    if interact and named:
        terms.append(f'{treatment} x {named[0]}')
    terms.extend(named)

    def design(treated: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Returns the regression's columns with strata's means removed.

        Args:
            treated: the treatment of each vote.

        Returns:
            The treatment, its product with the first control (if
                interacted), and the controls, each less the mean of
                its stratum.

        """
        columns = [treated]
        if interact and named:
            columns.append(treated * others[:, 0])
        raw = np.column_stack([*columns, others])
        return _strata.demean(raw, stratum)

    x = design(dose)
    centered = _strata.demean(y, stratum)
    coefficients, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(x, centered, rcond = None)
    errors = _clustered_errors(
        x, centered - x @ coefficients, groups,
        absorbed = int(stratum.max()) + 1)
    tested = 2 if interact and named else 1
    reassigned = _randomization_p_values(
        coefficients[:tested], dose = dose, stratum = stratum,
        centered = centered, design = design,
        n_permutations = n_permutations, seed = seed)
    t_statistics = np.divide(
        coefficients, errors, out = np.full_like(coefficients, np.nan),
        where = errors > 0)
    table = pd.DataFrame({
        'coefficient': coefficients,
        'std_error': errors,
        't_statistic': t_statistics,
        'p_value': [
            math.erfc(abs(t) / math.sqrt(2)) if np.isfinite(t)
            else np.nan for t in t_statistics],
        'ri_p_value': [
            *reassigned, *[np.nan] * (len(terms) - tested)],
        'ci_lower': coefficients - _Z_95 * errors,
        'ci_upper': coefficients + _Z_95 * errors},
        index = pd.Index(terms, name = 'term'))
    fitted = {
        'terms': terms, 'coefficients': coefficients, 'errors': errors}
    details = {
        'tool': 'courtpy (least squares with fixed effects)',
        'outcome': outcome,
        'treatment': treatment,
        'controls': named,
        'strata': grouped,
        'votes': int(kept.sum()),
        'clusters': int(groups.max()) + 1,
        'n_permutations': n_permutations}
    return amos.inferers.Inference(
        table = table, fitted = fitted, details = details)

docs.text:
Tables of reference data that describe something other than cases.

Each module downloads, reads, and merges one kind of reference data: the judges (judges), the federal courts (courts), the Supreme Court Database (scdb), the Federal Judicial Center's Integrated Database (fjc_idb), the Judicial Common Space (jcs), the political context of each case (politics), and scores of judges and courts from training data (scores). Each can also be imported from courtpy itself (such as courtpy.judges).

docs.title: courts
docs.text:
The courts of each jurisdiction, and the circuit of each federal case.

The table of a jurisdiction's courts is "courts.csv" in its folder of "instructions" (such as "instructions/federal/courts.csv"), which can be opened in a spreadsheet, with one row for each court:

Column Meaning court_num courtpy's number for the court: 1 to 13 for the courts of appeals (12 for the D.C. Circuit and 13 for the Federal Circuit), as the rules that make "court_num" for cases number them, 99 for the Supreme Court, 101 and up for specialized and historical courts (such as the bankruptcy appellate panels), and 1001 and up for the district courts. court A name for the court that can be a folder's name (such as "southern_district_of_new_york", or "scotus" for the Supreme Court). feature_name The court's name as a label for tables and plots (such as "Southern District of New York"). level "high", "appellate", "trial", or "specialty", which state courts will share. circuit_num The number of the court of appeals that hears its appeals (for a district court, that of its state, as fjc-biographies numbers them). courtlistener_name CourtListener's id for the court (such as "nysd"), if it has one. fjc_name A regular expression for the Federal Judicial Center's names for the court, matched ignoring case. Several names are separated by a vertical bar. opinion_name A regular expression for how an opinion names the court (its name, or its abbreviation in a citation, such as "S.D.N.Y.", "S. D. N.Y.", or "S.D. New York"), matched ignoring case. The header rules of a source whose cases name their court in text (such as Lexis-Nexis) find "court_num" and "court_name" with it, and then with fjc_name, and every source's header rules find the trial or specialized court whose decision is reviewed in the history the same way ("lower_court_num" and "lower_court_name"; see courtpy.rules.make_court_rules).

The header rules have no names of courts of their own, so a court added to the table is found in cases without changing any rules. CourtListener cases find "court_num" and "court_name" by CourtListener's id for the court instead (see court_numbers_by_courtlistener_name and court_names_by_courtlistener_name), and "lower_court_num" and "lower_court_name" by the id of the court appealed from, if the docket has it.

circuits finds the circuit of each case in a table of cases, which add_circuit uses.

Contents

circuits: returns the number of the circuit of each case. court_labels: returns the label of each case's court for tables and plots, in the order of the table of courts. court_names_by_courtlistener_name: returns courtpy's name for each court, by CourtListener's id for it. court_numbers_by_courtlistener_name: returns courtpy's number for each court, by CourtListener's id for it. court_table: returns the table of a jurisdiction's courts. federal_courts: returns the table of the federal courts. _COURTS_FILE_NAME: the name of the file of each jurisdiction's courts.
