def fetch(self, kind: str) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Downloads one bulk file, resuming a download that was interrupted.

    The file is downloaded with `amos.loaders.download_file`, which
    writes it beside its path (with ".part" added) until it is whole, so
    a file in `folder` is always complete.

    Args:
        kind: "courts", "dockets", "opinion-clusters", "citations", or
            "opinions".

    Raises:
        OSError: if the download stopped before the whole file arrived
            (run it again to resume).
        requests.HTTPError: if the file cannot be downloaded.

    Returns:
        The path of the downloaded file.

    """
    name = self._name(kind)
    assert isinstance(self.folder, pathlib.Path)  # noqa: S101
    path = self.folder / name
    if not path.is_file():
        logger.info('downloading %s to %s', name, self.folder)
    return amos.loaders.download_file(
        self._url(kind),
        path,
        timeout = self.timeout,
        session = self.session,
        resume = True)

def resolve_date(self) -> str:
    """Returns `date`, finding the newest complete set of files if needed.

    Returns:
        The date of the files to use, as YYYY-MM-DD.

    Raises:
        LookupError: if no date has every kind of file that courtpy needs.

    """
    if self.date is None:
        common: set[str] | None = None
        for kind in _KINDS:
            dates = set(self.available(kind))
            common = dates if common is None else common & dates
        if not common:
            message = 'no date in the bulk data has every file needed'
            raise LookupError(message)
        self.date = max(common)
    return self.date

def rows(
    self,
    kind: str,
    *,
    columns: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    keep: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Iterator[dict[str, str]]:
    """Yields chosen rows of one bulk file.

    Args:
        kind: "courts", "dockets", "opinion-clusters", "citations", or
            "opinions".
        columns: the columns to return. Defaults to `None`, which
            returns every column.
        keep: the values to keep of each of some columns (see `chunks`).
            Defaults to `None`, which keeps every row.

    Yields:
        dict[str, str]: each row, mapping column names to text. Missing
            values are empty `str`s.

    """
    for chunk in self.chunks(kind, columns = columns, keep = keep):
        for row in chunk.to_dict('records'):
            yield {str(key): value for key, value in row.items()}

docs.title: courtlistener
docs.text:
Downloads court opinions from the CourtListener API and reads them.

CourtListener (https://www.courtlistener.com) is a free legal research site run by the Free Law Project. Its opinions can be downloaded in two ways:

  • The REST API, with CourtListener, which needs an API key (see courtpy.secrets). It is best for small or very recent sets of cases, because CourtListener limits how many requests an account can make (a free account can make 5 a minute, 50 an hour, and 125 a day, as of 2026). CourtListener waits when asked to, saves its place, and resumes where it stopped when it is run again.
  • The bulk data files, with courtpy.bulk.BulkData, which need no key and have no limits, but are very large and are updated every three months.

Both save each case as a JSON file named for its CourtListener cluster id, in a folder named for its court (such as "courtlistener/ca1/4567890.json"), which read_case turns into a Case for parsing.

Contents

ApiDownload: downloads cases with the API ("download = api"). CourtListener: a client for the CourtListener REST API. CourtListenerSource: reads cases saved by CourtListener or courtpy.bulk.BulkData. CourtListenerError: raised when the API returns an error. RateLimitError: raised when the API asks for a longer pause than allowed. add_opinions: adds opinions to a saved case. case_path: returns the path of a saved case. citation_strings: returns citations as text. is_complete: returns whether a case was saved with its opinions. opinion_role: classifies an opinion as majority, concurrence, or dissent. opinion_text: returns the plain text of an opinion. read_case: reads a saved case for parsing. save_case: saves a case. slim_opinion: keeps one field of an opinion's text, to save space. logger: the module's logger, which reports the progress of downloads and pauses asked for by CourtListener.

A client for the CourtListener REST API (version 4).

Every request includes the API key, which is found with courtpy.secrets.get_api_key if it is not passed. Requests are spaced at least min_interval seconds apart. def download(
    self,
    courts: str | Iterable[str],
    start_date: str | None = None,
    end_date: str | None = None,
    folder: pathlib.Path | str = 'courtlistener',
    *,
    max_cases: int | None = None,
    dockets: bool = False,
    overwrite: bool = False) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Downloads the cases of `courts` filed between two dates.

    Each page of cases (opinion clusters) takes one request, and their
    opinions take one more (or more, if they have many opinions). Cases
    that were already saved (with their opinions) are skipped, and the
    place in each court's list of cases is saved, so running a download
    again resumes it. Running a finished download again takes one request
    for each court and saves any cases added to CourtListener since.

    Args:
        courts: CourtListener court ids (such as "ca1") or names of groups
            of them (such as "federal_appellate").
        start_date: earliest date filed, as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to `None`
            (no earliest date).
        end_date: latest date filed, as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to `None` (no
            latest date).
        folder: folder to save the cases in. Defaults to "courtlistener".
        max_cases: most cases to save in each court in this run. Defaults
            to `None` (every case).
        dockets: whether to also download each case's docket (every
            field but those in `options._DOCKET_SKIPPED`, such as its
            docket number, dates, and the court appealed from). This
            takes one more request for each case. Defaults to `False`.
            The bulk data always includes the docket.
        overwrite: whether to download cases that were already saved.
            Defaults to `False`.

    Raises:
        RateLimitError: if CourtListener asks for a pause longer than
            `max_wait`. What was downloaded is kept.

    Returns:
        The paths of the cases saved in this run.

    """
    folder = pathlib.Path(folder)
    saved: list[pathlib.Path] = []
    for court in utilities.expand_courts(courts):
        saved.extend(self._download_court(
            court, start_date, end_date, folder,
            max_cases = max_cases, dockets = dockets,
            overwrite = overwrite))
    logger.info(
        'saved %d cases in %s with %d requests', len(saved), folder,
        self.requests_made)
    return saved

def get(
    self,
    path: str,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns the JSON response of one request to the API.

    Args:
        path: a path in the API (such as "clusters/") or a full address
            (such as the "next" page of a response).
        params: query parameters. Defaults to `None`.

    Raises:
        CourtListenerError: if the API returns an error, rejects the key,
            or cannot be reached after several tries.
        RateLimitError: if the API asks for a pause longer than
            `max_wait`.

    Returns:
        The decoded JSON.

    """
    url = path if path.startswith('http') else urllib.parse.urljoin(
        self.base_url, path)
    failures = 0
    while True:
        self._space_requests()
        try:
            response = self.session.get(
                url, params = params, timeout = self.timeout)
        except requests.RequestException as error:
            failures += 1
            if failures > _RETRIES:
                message = f'CourtListener could not be reached: {error}'
                raise CourtListenerError(message) from error
            time.sleep(5 * 2 ** failures)
            continue
        finally:
            self.requests_made += 1
            self._last_request = time.monotonic()
        status = response.status_code
        if status == 429:
            wait = _retry_after(response)
            if wait > self.max_wait:
                raise RateLimitError(wait)
            logger.info(
                'CourtListener asked for a pause: waiting %.0f seconds',
                wait)
            time.sleep(wait)
            continue
        if status in _TEMPORARY and failures < _RETRIES:
            failures += 1
            time.sleep(5 * 2 ** failures)
            continue
        if status in (401, 403):
            message = (
                f'CourtListener rejected the request ({status}). Check '
                f'the API key with "courtpy key show". Details: '
                f'{_detail(response)}'
            )
            raise CourtListenerError(message)
        if status >= 400:
            message = (
                f'CourtListener returned {status}: {_detail(response)}')
            raise CourtListenerError(message)
        return dict(response.json())

def pages(
    self,
    path: str,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Iterator[
        tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], str | None]]:
    """Yields the results of each page of a list, and the next address.

    Args:
        path: a path in the API (such as "clusters/") or the address of a
            page.
        params: query parameters for the first page. Defaults to `None`.

    Yields:
        tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], str | None]: the results on each page
            and the address of the next page (or `None` after the last
            page).

    """
    url: str | None = path
    query = params
    while url:
        data = self.get(url, query)
        next_url = data.get('next')
        yield list(data.get('results', [])), next_url
        url, query = next_url, None

def add_opinions(
    path: pathlib.Path,
    opinions: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> None:
    """Adds opinions to a saved case, replacing any with the same id.

    Args:
        path: path of the saved case.

    record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding = 'utf-8'))
    existing = {o.get('id'): o for o in record.get('opinions', [])}

def citation_strings(citations: Iterable[Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Returns citations as text, such as "123 F.3d 456".

    Args:
        citations: citations from CourtListener: `dict`s with "volume",
            "reporter", and "page", or text.

    Returns:
        The citations as text.

    """
    found = []
    for citation in citations or []:
        if isinstance(citation, Mapping):
            parts = (citation.get(k) for k in ('volume', 'reporter', 'page'))
            text = ' '.join(str(p) for p in parts if p not in (None, ''))
        else:
            text = str(citation)
        if text.strip():
            found.append(text.strip())
    return found

def is_complete(path: pathlib.Path) -> bool:
    """Returns whether a case was saved with at least one opinion.

    Args:
        path: path of a saved case.

    Returns:
        Whether the file exists, can be read, and has an opinion.

    if not path.is_file():

    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return False
    return bool(record.get('opinions'))

def opinion_role(kind: str | None) -> str:
    """Classifies an opinion by its CourtListener type.

    Args:
        kind: the opinion's "type", such as "010combined", "020lead",
            "030concurrence", "035concurrenceinpart", or "040dissent".

    Returns:
        "majority" (combined, lead, unanimous, or plurality opinions, and
            opinions without a type), "concurrence", "dissent", "mixed" (an
            opinion concurring in part and dissenting in part), or "other"
            (such as an addendum).

    """
    text = (kind or '').lower()
    if not text:
        return 'majority'
    for fragment, role in _ROLES:
        if fragment in text:
            return role
    return 'other'

The sections of text have the same names as the sections that rules find in Lexis-Nexis cases (such as "party", "history", "counsel", and "judges"), so that the same rules work for both. "court_num" and "court_name" are courtpy's number and name for the case's court, found by CourtListener's id for it in the table of courts of options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION (see courtpy.courts.court_numbers_by_courtlistener_name), and "lower_court_num" and "lower_court_name" are those of the court appealed from, by the docket's id for it. Each is None if the table does not have the court (the header rules then look for the court appealed from in the history).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path Path | str

path of a case saved by CourtListener or BulkData.

required

Type Description Case

Source code in src/courtpy/sources/courtlistener.py 
def read_case(path: pathlib.Path | str) -> cases.Case:
    """Reads a saved CourtListener case for parsing.

    The sections of text have the same names as the sections that rules find
    in Lexis-Nexis cases (such as "party", "history", "counsel", and
    "judges"), so that the same rules work for both. "court_num" and
    "court_name" are courtpy's number and name for the case's court, found
    by CourtListener's id for it in the table of courts of
    `options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION` (see
    `courtpy.courts.court_numbers_by_courtlistener_name`), and
    "lower_court_num" and "lower_court_name" are those of the court appealed
    from, by the docket's id for it. Each is `None` if the table does not
    have the court (the header rules then look for the court appealed from
    in the history).

    Args:
        path: path of a case saved by `CourtListener` or `BulkData`.

    Returns:
        The case.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding = 'utf-8'))
    cluster = record.get('cluster') or {}
    docket = record.get('docket') or {}
    court = record.get('court') or {}
    opinions = sorted(
        record.get('opinions') or [],
        key = lambda o: (
            o.get('ordering_key') is None, o.get('ordering_key') or 0,
            str(o.get('type') or ''), o.get('id') or 0))
    roles = [opinion_role(o.get('type')) for o in opinions]

    def authors(*kinds: str) -> str:
        """Returns the authors of the case's opinions with some roles.

        Args:
            *kinds: roles of opinions (see `opinion_role`), such as
                "majority" or "dissent".

        Returns:
            The "author_str" of each opinion with one of those roles, one per
                line, leaving out blank ones.

        """
        return '\n'.join(
            str(o.get('author_str') or '').strip()
            for o, role in zip(opinions, roles, strict = True)
            if role in kinds and str(o.get('author_str') or '').strip())

    majority = [
        o for o, role in zip(opinions, roles, strict = True)
        if role == 'majority']
    texts = [opinion_text(o) for o in opinions]
    sections = {
        'party': _first(
            cluster.get('case_name_full'), docket.get('case_name_full'),
            cluster.get('case_name')),
        'court': _first(court.get('full_name'), court.get('id')),
        'docket_number': _first(docket.get('docket_number')),
        'citation': '; '.join(record.get('citations') or []),
        'history': '\n'.join(_texts(
            cluster.get('procedural_history'), cluster.get('history'),
            docket.get('appeal_from_str'))),
        'counsel': _first(cluster.get('attorneys')),
        'disposition': _first(cluster.get('disposition')),
        'judges': _first(cluster.get('judges'), docket.get('panel_str')),
        'opinion_by': authors('majority'),
        'concurring_lines': authors('concurrence', 'mixed'),
        'dissenting_lines': authors('dissent', 'mixed'),
        'posture': _first(cluster.get('posture')),
        'syllabus': _first(cluster.get('syllabus')),
        'opinion': '\n\n'.join(t for t in texts if t)}
    sections = {
        k: amos.mungers.html_to_text(v) if '<' in v else v
        for k, v in sections.items() if v}
    date_filed = _first(cluster.get('date_filed'))
    status = _first(cluster.get('precedential_status'))
    court_id = court.get('id') or docket.get('court_id')
    lower_id = _court_id_from(
        docket.get('appeal_from_id') or docket.get('appeal_from'))
    numbers = courts.court_numbers_by_courtlistener_name(
        options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION)
    names = courts.court_names_by_courtlistener_name(
        options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {
        'source': 'courtlistener',
        'cluster_id': cluster.get('id'),
        'docket_id': cluster.get('docket_id') or docket.get('id') or (
            _id_from_url(cluster.get('docket'))),
        'court': court_id,
        'court_num': numbers.get(str(court_id or '').lower()),
        'court_name': names.get(str(court_id or '').lower()),
        'lower_court_num': numbers.get(lower_id or ''),
        'lower_court_name': names.get(lower_id or ''),
        'case_name': _first(cluster.get('case_name')),
        'docket_number': sections.get('docket_number'),
        'citation': sections.get('citation'),
        'disposition': sections.get('disposition'),
        'judges': sections.get('judges'),
        'date_filed': date_filed or None,
        'date_argued': _first(docket.get('date_argued')) or None,
        'year': int(date_filed[:4]) if date_filed[:4].isdigit() else None,
        'precedential_status': status or None,
        'published': status.lower() == 'published' if status else None,
        'per_curiam': any(_true(o.get('per_curiam')) for o in majority),
        'opinions': len(opinions),
        'author_id': next(
            (o.get('author_id') for o in majority if o.get('author_id')), None),
        'panel_ids': [
            i for i in (_id_from_url(p) for p in cluster.get('panel') or [])
            if i is not None],
        'citation_count': cluster.get('citation_count'),
        'nature_of_suit': _first(
            cluster.get('nature_of_suit'), docket.get('nature_of_suit'))
            or None,
        'url': _url(cluster)}
    # Only cases of the Supreme Court have an id in the Supreme Court
    # Database, so other tables of cases get no column for it.
    if _first(cluster.get('scdb_id')):
        metadata['scdb_id'] = _first(cluster.get('scdb_id'))
    return cases.Case(
        id = str(cluster.get('id') or path.stem),
        source = 'courtlistener',
        sections = sections,
        metadata = metadata,
        path = path)

def save_case(path: pathlib.Path, record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Saves a case as a JSON file, replacing any file at `path` safely.

    Args:
        path: path to save the case to. Its folder is created if needed.

def slim_opinion(opinion: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns an opinion with only one field of text, to save space.

    Args:
        opinion: an opinion from the API or the bulk data.

    Returns:
        The fields in `_OPINION_KEPT` that it has, and the first field in
            `options._TEXT_FIELDS` that is not blank.

    """
    slim = {k: opinion[k] for k in _OPINION_KEPT if k in opinion}
    if 'cluster_id' not in slim:
        slim['cluster_id'] = _cluster_id(opinion)
    for field in options._TEXT_FIELDS:
        value = opinion.get(field)
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
            slim[field] = value
            break
    return slim

docs.title: lexis
docs.text:
Reads court opinions downloaded from Lexis-Nexis as text files.

Lexis-Nexis lets users download many cases at once in one text file, with a line such as "3 of 250 DOCUMENTS" before each case. split divides such files into one file for each case, which read_case reads for parsing.

Lexis-Nexis cases have a header (with the parties, court, docket number, dates, history, counsel, judges, and so on) followed by the opinions. The rules in the "lexis_nexis" rulebook (in "instructions/sources/lexis_nexis", with a file for each kind of court) find each part of the header, and the "lexis_nexis_header" rulebook (with that folder's "header.csv") finds the court, parties, and judges in the parts, so they can be changed without changing courtpy.

Contents

LexisNexisSource: reads Lexis-Nexis cases saved one to a text file. clean: removes common clutter from Lexis-Nexis text. finish: adds dates and publication status to a parsed case. read_case: reads a Lexis-Nexis case for parsing. split: divides files of many cases into one file for each case. logger: the module's logger, which reports how many cases each file held.

Removes common clutter from Lexis-Nexis text.

Star paging ("*123"), bracketed footnote numbers ("[12]"), and the "Signal:" and "As of:" lines that Lexis adds are removed, spaces are collapsed, and spaces at the starts and ends of lines are trimmed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default text str

text of one or more cases.

required

Returns:

Type Description str

The cleaned text.

Source code in src/courtpy/sources/lexis.py 
def clean(text: str) -> str:
    """Removes common clutter from Lexis-Nexis text.

    Star paging ("*123"), bracketed footnote numbers ("[12]"), and the
    "Signal:" and "As of:" lines that Lexis adds are removed, spaces are
    collapsed, and spaces at the starts and ends of lines are trimmed.

    Args:
        text: text of one or more cases.

    Returns:
        The cleaned text.

    """
    text = text.replace('\r\n', '\n').replace('\r', '\n')
    text = text.replace('*', '')
    text = re.sub(r'\[\d*\]', '', text)
    text = re.sub(r'[^\S\n]+', ' ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'(?im)^ ?(?:signal|as of):.*\n?\n?', '', text)
    return re.sub(r' *\n *', '\n', text)

Adds dates and publication status to a parsed Lexis-Nexis case.

The "dates" section has each line of the header with a date (such as "March 3, 2009, Argued"), with "; " between them. Each kind of date (decided, filed, argued, submitted, and amended) is stored as an ISO date in its own column ("date_decided" and so on). "date_filed" is the date filed or, if there is none, the date decided, as on CourtListener. "year" is the year of that date (or of the first date found).

A case is published if it has a Federal Reporter citation and no notice that it is unpublished (as found by the federal rules).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default row MutableMapping[str, Any]

a parsed case.

required

Returns:

Type Description MutableMapping[str, Any]

The same row, with the new columns.

def finish(row: MutableMapping[str, Any]) -> MutableMapping[str, Any]:
    """Adds dates and publication status to a parsed Lexis-Nexis case.

    The "dates" section has each line of the header with a date (such as
    "March 3, 2009, Argued"), with "; " between them. Each kind of date
    (decided, filed, argued, submitted, and amended) is stored as an ISO date
    in its own column ("date_decided" and so on). "date_filed" is the date
    filed or, if there is none, the date decided, as on CourtListener. "year"
    is the year of that date (or of the first date found).

    A case is published if it has a Federal Reporter citation and no notice
    that it is unpublished (as found by the federal rules).

    Args:
        row: a parsed case.

    Returns:
        The same `row`, with the new columns.

    """
    lines = str(row.get('dates') or '').split(cases._SEPARATOR)
    for kind in _DATE_KINDS:
        column = f'date_{kind.lower()}'
        row.setdefault(column, None)
        for line in lines:
            if kind in line.upper():
                row[column] = utilities.parse_date(line)
                break
    if not row.get('date_filed'):
        row['date_filed'] = row.get('date_decided')
    first = row.get('date_filed') or next(
        (d for d in map(utilities.parse_date, lines) if d), None)
    row['year'] = int(first[:4]) if first else None
    if 'cite_federal_reporter' in row:
        row['published'] = bool(row['cite_federal_reporter']) and not bool(
            row.get('notice_unpublished'))
    return row

def split(
    files: Iterable[pathlib.Path | str] | pathlib.Path | str,
    folder: pathlib.Path | str = 'lexis_nexis') -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Divides files of many cases into one file for each case.

    Args:
        files: text files downloaded from Lexis-Nexis, or a folder of them.
        folder: folder to save the cases in. Each is named for the file it came
            from and its place in that file (such as "batch1_00003.txt").
            Defaults to "lexis_nexis".

    Returns:
        The paths of the new files.

    """
    if isinstance(files, str | pathlib.Path):
        source = pathlib.Path(files)
        files = sorted(source.glob('*.txt')) if source.is_dir() else [source]
    folder = pathlib.Path(folder)
    folder.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    saved = []
    for file in files:
        file = pathlib.Path(file)  # noqa: PLW2901
        pieces = [clean(p).strip() for p in _DIVIDER.split(_read_text(file))]
        number = 0
        for piece in pieces:
            if not piece:
                continue
            number += 1
            path = folder / f'{file.stem}_{number:05d}.txt'
            path.write_text(piece + '\n', encoding = 'utf-8')
            saved.append(path)
        logger.info('%s: %d cases', file.name, number)
    return saved

docs.text:
courtpy's steps of the amos wrangler, which turn opinions into a table.

loaders collect cases into a project, rules and parsers find variables in their text, coders code what the rules found (such as who won), and shapers summarize cases by court, case type, and party type. Each can also be imported from courtpy itself (such as courtpy.parsers).

docs.title: coders
docs.text:
Techniques that code variables from parsed cases.

code_parties, code_case_type, code_outcome, split_values, and tidy_cases are amos.Munger techniques, which change and add columns without adding or removing rows, and drop_text_columns is an amos.Cleaner, which removes columns. Each is added to the amos (and chrisjen) library as soon as courtpy is imported, and it can be named in the settings of any amos worker. courtpy's loaders (see courtpy.loaders) also run the coders named in their "coders" parameter (by default, code_parties, code_case_type, and code_outcome, in that order) right after parsing, so that a label such as "outcome_reversal" exists when the data is loaded.

The coders use the columns made by the federal rules (such as "party1_appellant" and "disposition_reverse"). With other rules, make columns with the same names or write your own coder.

Contents

CodeCaseType: decides whether each case is criminal or civil, and its other types. CodeOutcome: decides whether each decision reversed the court below, and which side won. CodeParties: completes the roles of the parties. DropTextColumns: removes columns that models cannot use, such as text and lists. SplitValues: turns text with several values in each cell into lists or columns. TidyCases: gives columns of booleans or whole numbers with missing values types that allow them. code: applies coders (or other amos techniques) to parsed cases. _UNITED_STATES_FIRST: the pattern of a party's text that begins with the United States.

docs.title: CodeCaseType(contents=None, name='', parameters=dict()) dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: Munger

Decides whether each case is criminal or civil, and its other types.

A case is criminal ("type_criminal") if the United States is a party and there is a sign of a criminal case: a criminal docket number or history, a United States Attorney as counsel, or a criminal issue in the opinion (any "criminal_..." column). The United States is then the prosecution, and the other party is the criminal defendant. When both parties' text names the United States (as a caption that joins several appeals can: "Joseph Prochilo, Defendant, Appellee; United States of America, Appellant, v. Elvis Guerrero, Defendant, Appellee"), the party whose text ("party1" or "party2") begins with the United States is the prosecution, if only one does, and otherwise the party that is a defendant and not a plaintiff, if only one is, is the criminal defendant. Every other case is civil ("type_civil"), and its plaintiffs and defendants are coded as civil plaintiffs and defendants.

Each other prefix of the rules of the topics of cases (see rules.case_type_prefixes: "tort", "contract", "ip", "writ", and "constitutional" in courtpy's rules) is a case type too: "type_tort" is true if any "tort_..." column is. So a case can be of several types (a civil case that is a tort case and a contract case), and a prefix added to the rules (such as "immigration_") is a type once the cases are parsed with it. cases_to_case_types makes a table of the types.

Adds "type_criminal", "type_civil", "type_{prefix}" for each other prefix that a column of the cases has, and for each party, "party1_prosecution", "party1_criminal_defendant", "party1_civil_plaintiff", and "party1_civil_defendant" (and the same for "party2").

Needs "party1_united_states", "party2_united_states", "party1_plaintiff", "party2_plaintiff", "party1_defendant", and "party2_defendant". Uses "docket_criminal", "counsel_us_attorney", and the "criminal_..." columns if they exist.

def munge(
    self,
    data: pd.DataFrame,
    prefixes: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Codes the types of each case.

    Args:
        data: the parsed cases.
        prefixes: the prefixes of the columns of flags that are case
            types, other than "criminal" and "civil". Defaults to `None`,
            in which case they are those of courtpy's rules (see
            `rules.case_type_prefixes`).
        **kwargs: not used.

    Returns:
        The cases, with the new columns.

    """
    needed = [
        f'{side}_{role}' for side in ('party1', 'party2')
        for role in ('united_states', 'plaintiff', 'defendant')]
    _require_federal_columns(data, needed, self.name)
    signals = [
        c for c in data.columns
        if c in ('docket_criminal', 'counsel_us_attorney')
        or c.startswith('criminal_')]
    criminal_signal = pd.Series(False, index = data.index)
    for column in signals:
        criminal_signal |= cases.column_as_flags(data, column)
    government = (
        cases.column_as_flags(data, 'party1_united_states')
        | cases.column_as_flags(data, 'party2_united_states'))
    criminal = government & criminal_signal
    data['type_criminal'] = criminal
    data['type_civil'] = ~criminal
    chosen = (
        rules.case_type_prefixes() if prefixes is None
        else utilities.listify(prefixes))
    for prefix in chosen:
        flags = [c for c in data.columns if str(c).startswith(f'{prefix}_')]
        if prefix in ('criminal', 'civil') or not flags:
            continue
        found = pd.Series(False, index = data.index)
        for column in flags:
            found |= cases.column_as_flags(data, column)
        data[f'type_{prefix}'] = found
    united_states = _prosecuting_sides(data)
    for side, other in _SIDES:
        prosecution = criminal & united_states[side]
        data[f'{side}_prosecution'] = prosecution
        data[f'{side}_criminal_defendant'] = (
            criminal & united_states[other] & ~prosecution)
        data[f'{side}_civil_plaintiff'] = ~criminal & (
            cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_plaintiff')
            | cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{other}_defendant'))
        data[f'{side}_civil_defendant'] = ~criminal & (
            cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_defendant')
            | cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{other}_plaintiff'))
    return data

docs.text:
Bases: Munger

Decides whether each decision reversed the court below, and who won.

A decision is a reversal ("outcome_reversal") if it reversed, vacated, or remanded. The disposition in the header (or in CourtListener's data) is used when there is one, because the opinion may mention reversals that are not its own. Otherwise, the decision that the opinion states ("AFFIRMED." or "we reverse", which the federal rules find as "decision") is used. Only when there is neither are the opinion's words anywhere ("reverse", "vacate", or "remand") used, which may be about an earlier decision or a standard of review ("we will reverse only if").

Then, for each party whose role is known (see CodeParties), the party won ("outcome_party1_won") if it brought the appeal and the decision was reversed, or it defended the appeal and the decision was not reversed. With CodeCaseType, the winner is also coded by side: "outcome_criminal_defendant_won", "outcome_prosecution_won", "outcome_civil_plaintiff_won", and "outcome_civil_defendant_won", and "appeal_by_defendant" says whether the (criminal or civil) defendant brought the appeal.

Values that cannot be known (such as who won when neither party's role is known, or whether the criminal defendant won a civil case) are missing (pd.NA). Filter the cases before using such a column as a label (for example, with the filter_rows technique and the query "type_criminal").

Needs "disposition_reverse", "disposition_vacate", "disposition_remand", "opinion_reverse", "opinion_vacate", and "opinion_remand". Uses "disposition", "decision", "decision_reverse", "decision_vacate", and "decision_remand", and the columns made by CodeParties and CodeCaseType, if they exist.

def munge(self, data: pd.DataFrame, **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Codes the outcome of each decision.

    Args:
        data: the parsed cases.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Returns:
        The cases, with the new columns.

    """
    rulings = ('reverse', 'vacate', 'remand')
    _require_federal_columns(
        data,
        [f'{p}_{r}' for p in ('disposition', 'opinion') for r in rulings],
        self.name)
    header = pd.Series(False, index = data.index)
    decision = pd.Series(False, index = data.index)
    opinion = pd.Series(False, index = data.index)
    for ruling in rulings:
        header |= cases.column_as_flags(data, f'disposition_{ruling}')
        decision |= cases.column_as_flags(data, f'decision_{ruling}')
        opinion |= cases.column_as_flags(data, f'opinion_{ruling}')
    reversal = header.where(
        _has_text(data, 'disposition'),
        decision.where(_has_text(data, 'decision'), opinion))
    data['outcome_reversal'] = reversal
    if not {'party1_appealing', 'party2_appealing'} <= set(data.columns):
        return data
    won = {}
    for side, _ in _SIDES:
        outcome = pd.Series(pd.NA, index = data.index, dtype = 'boolean')
        appealing = cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_appealing')
        defending = cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_defending')
        outcome[appealing] = reversal[appealing]
        outcome[defending] = ~reversal[defending]
        won[side] = outcome
        data[f'outcome_{side}_won'] = outcome
    categories = {
        'criminal_defendant': 'criminal_defendant',
        'prosecution': 'prosecution',
        'civil_plaintiff': 'civil_plaintiff',
        'civil_defendant': 'civil_defendant'}
    if all(f'party1_{c}' in data.columns for c in categories.values()):
        for name, column in categories.items():
            outcome = pd.Series(
                pd.NA, index = data.index, dtype = 'boolean')
            for side, _ in _SIDES:
                present = cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_{column}')
                outcome[present] = won[side][present]
            data[f'outcome_{name}_won'] = outcome
        by_defendant = pd.Series(
            pd.NA, index = data.index, dtype = 'boolean')
        for side, _ in _SIDES:
            defendant = (
                cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_criminal_defendant')
                | cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_civil_defendant'))
            known = defendant & (
                cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_appealing')
                | cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_defending'))
            appealing = cases.column_as_flags(data, f'{side}_appealing')
            by_defendant[known] = appealing[known]
        data['appeal_by_defendant'] = by_defendant
    return data

docs.text:
Bases: Munger

Completes the roles of the parties and finds who brought the appeal.

A caption often gives one party's role but not the other's ("United States v. Smith, Defendant-Appellant"). Because the roles in each pair are opposites, a party is coded as an appellee if the other party is an appellant (and so on for petitioners and respondents, and for plaintiffs and defendants).

It also adds "party1_appealing" and "party2_appealing" (the party brought the appeal) and "party1_defending" and "party2_defending" (the other party did). Each party's own caption decides first: a party is appealing if it is an appellant and not an appellee, and defending if the reverse. Only a party named neither appellant nor appellee is judged by whether it is a petitioner or respondent, since a habeas petitioner who won below is the appellee ("Petitioner, Appellee"). A party whose own caption decides nothing, or names it both (as a caption that joins several appeals can: "Joseph Prochilo, Defendant, Appellee; United States of America, Appellant, v. Elvis Guerrero, Defendant, Appellee"), takes the opposite of the other party's, if the other party's caption decides it. If both captions decide and agree, both are kept, and if they disagree (both appellants, as in a cross-appeal), both are unknown. Both are false for a party whose role is unknown.

Needs the columns "party1_{role}" and "party2_{role}" for each role: appellant, appellee, petitioner, respondent, plaintiff, and defendant.

def munge(self, data: pd.DataFrame, **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Completes the roles of the parties.

    Args:
        data: the parsed cases.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Returns:
        The cases, with completed roles.

    """
    roles = [r for pair in _OPPOSITES for r in pair]
    needed = [f'{s}_{r}' for s in ('party1', 'party2') for r in roles]
    _require_federal_columns(data, needed, self.name)
    original = {c: cases.column_as_flags(data, c) for c in needed}
    for first, second in _OPPOSITES:
        for side, other in _SIDES:
            data[f'{side}_{first}'] = (
                original[f'{side}_{first}'] | original[f'{other}_{second}'])
            data[f'{side}_{second}'] = (
                original[f'{side}_{second}'] | original[f'{other}_{first}'])
    own = {side: _own_direction(original, side) for side, _ in _SIDES}
    for side, other in _SIDES:
        mine_appealing, mine_defending = own[side]
        other_appealing, other_defending = own[other]
        mine_known = mine_appealing | mine_defending
        other_known = other_appealing | other_defending
        agree = (
            (mine_appealing & other_defending)
            | (mine_defending & other_appealing))
        data[f'{side}_appealing'] = (
            (mine_appealing & (agree | ~other_known))
            | (~mine_known & other_defending))
        data[f'{side}_defending'] = (
            (mine_defending & (agree | ~other_known))
            | (~mine_known & other_appealing))
    return data

def clean(
    self,
    data: pd.DataFrame,
    keep: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    label: str | None = None,
    groups: Sequence[str] = (),
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Removes columns of text and lists.

    Args:
        data: the cases.
        keep: names of columns to keep even if they hold text. Defaults to
            `None`.
        label: name of the label, which is always kept. Defaults to
            `None`.
        groups: names of the group columns, which are always kept.
            Defaults to an empty tuple.
        **kwargs: not used.

    Returns:
        The cases, without text and lists.

    """
    names = [keep] if isinstance(keep, str) else list(keep or [])
    missing = [c for c in names if c not in data.columns]
    if missing:
        message = f'the columns {missing} are not in the data'
        raise KeyError(message)
    kept = {*names, *(c for c in [label, *groups] if c)}
    dropped = [
        c for c in data.columns
        if c not in kept and _is_text(data[c])]
    return data.drop(columns = dropped)

Bases: Munger

Turns text with several values in each cell into lists or columns.

Rules that find several values in a case (names, matches, and categories rules, such as "panel_judges", "citations_case", and "agencies") write them as text, with "; " between them. With "into" set to "lists" (the default), each cell becomes a list of its values, and a cell without values an empty list. With "columns", each value gets a column of its own, named for the column and the value's place ("panel_judges_1", "panel_judges_2", and so on, for as many values as the row with the most has), and the text is kept.

To make a row for each value instead, use the lists_to_rows technique of amos (with "separator" set to ";").

def munge(
    self,
    data: pd.DataFrame,
    columns: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    separator: str = cases._SEPARATOR,
    into: str = 'lists',
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Splits the values of each cell of `columns`.

    Args:
        data: the cases.
        columns: names of the columns to split. Defaults to `None`, in
            which case they are the columns of the `names`, `matches`,
            and `categories` rules of the federal rulebook that are in
            the data.
        separator: the text between the values. Defaults to "; ", as the
            federal rules write them.
        into: "lists" or "columns". Defaults to "lists".
        **kwargs: not used.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if a column is not in the data.
        ValueError: if `into` is not "lists" or "columns".

    Returns:
        The cases, with lists in place of the text or with new columns.

    """
    if into not in _SPLIT_INTO:
        message = f'into must be one of {list(_SPLIT_INTO)}, not {into!r}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if columns is None:
        names = [c for c in _several_values() if c in data.columns]
    else:
        names = utilities.listify(columns)
    _require_federal_columns(data, names, self.name)
    added: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for column in names:
        values = [
            cases.split_cell(v, separator) for v in data[column].tolist()]
        if into == 'lists':
            data[column] = pd.Series(
                values, index = data.index, dtype = object)
            continue
        wide = pd.DataFrame(values, index = data.index, dtype = object)
        wide.columns = [f'{column}_{n + 1}' for n in range(wide.shape[1])]
        added.append(wide)
    if added:
        data = pd.concat([data, *added], axis = 1)
    return data

def code(
    data: pd.DataFrame | amos.Dataset,
    coders: str | Sequence[str] | None = options._DEFAULT_CODERS,
    *,
    parameters: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None) -> amos.Dataset:
    """Applies coders (or other `amos` techniques) to parsed cases.

    Args:
        data: the parsed cases, or a dataset of them (which is changed in
            place).
        coders: names of the techniques to apply, in order. Defaults to
            `options._DEFAULT_CODERS`. "none" (or `None`) applies none.
        parameters: parameters for the techniques, by their names. Defaults
            to `None`.

    Returns:
        A dataset of the coded cases, whose history records each technique:
            `Cases` made from a table, or the kind that the last shaper made
            (such as `Votes`, after "cases_to_votes").

    """
    dataset = (
        data if isinstance(data, amos.Dataset)
        else datasets.Cases.create(data))
    for name in utilities.listify(coders):
        if utilities.is_none_setting(name):
            continue
        kind = cast(
            'type[amos.Operation]',
            chrisjen.library.borrow(name, genre = 'operation'))
        settings = dict((parameters or {}).get(name, {}))
        technique = kind(parameters = settings)
        dataset = technique.apply(dataset)
    return dataset

docs.title: loaders
docs.text:
Techniques that load court cases into an amos project.

Loaders make a project's data from a source named in its settings, so a project with a loader needs no item. They are usually the first step of the wrangler, and they work through the project's clerk (its nagata.FileManager): a folder or file named by a relative path is looked for in the current folder and then in the clerk's input folder (the "input_folder" of the "files" section), and downloads are saved in the input folder.

courtpy's loaders collect court cases (downloading or dividing them first, if asked), parse them with rulebooks, and code them, so the label of a study (such as "outcome_reversal", which a coder makes) exists when the data is loaded:

[general]
seed = 43
label = outcome_reversal

[files]
input_folder = data

[appeals_project]
appeals_workers = wrangler, analyst, critic

[wrangler]
techniques = load_court_listener, drop_text_columns

[load_court_listener_parameters]
source = courtlistener
download = bulk
courts = federal_circuits
start_date = 2019-01-01
end_date = 2019-12-31
save = cases.csv
reuse = true

Every loader takes these parameters, set in its "{name}_parameters" section:

Parameter Meaning source The folder of saved cases (or, for load_cases, a saved table). coders Techniques to apply after parsing. Defaults to "code_parties, code_case_type, code_outcome" ("none" for load_cases). Use "none" for none. save File to save the coded table to (".csv", ".parquet", or ".xlsx"), with the whole dataset beside it in a joblib file of the same name (see Cases.save). A relative path is in the clerk's interim folder. reuse Whether to load the saved dataset, if there is one, instead of collecting, parsing, and coding the cases again. Defaults to false. label, task, groups As in amos: they default to those in the "general" section.

Other modules add reference loaders (see ReferenceLoader), which load a table that describes something other than cases. Each "load_" technique loads the files that courtpy keeps (or a file named as its "source"), and each "download_" technique downloads the files first, again if "refresh" is true:

Technique Table Module load_roster, download_biographies A roster of judges. courtpy.judges load_scdb, download_scdb The Supreme Court Database's cases or votes. courtpy.scdb load_idb, download_idb The Integrated Database's appeals. courtpy.fjc_idb load_politics, download_politics The political context of each year. courtpy.politics download_jcs The Judicial Common Space scores. courtpy.jcs Contents

CaseLoader: base class for techniques that load court cases. LoadCases: loads a dataset of cases saved by Cases.save, or a table of one. LoadCourtListener: collects, parses, and codes CourtListener cases. LoadLexisNexis: divides, parses, and codes Lexis-Nexis cases. ReferenceLoader: base class for techniques that load a table of reference data, such as load_scdb and download_biographies. SourceLoader: base class for loaders that download cases from a source (if asked) and parse them.

Bases: Loader, ABC

Base class for techniques that load court cases.

A subclass writes load, which collects and parses the cases at a source (a folder or file, already found with the clerk) and returns a table of them, one row for each case. apply then codes the table with the loader's "coders", saves it if "save" is set, and makes it the dataset that the rest of the workflow works on, with the label, task, and groups from the loader's parameters (which default to the "general" section of the settings). The label can be a column that a coder makes. If no coder makes it, it is pending, as in amos: a later technique (such as "derive_columns") can still make it, and using it before then raises an error. The dataset's history records the loader and then each coder.

The dataset is Cases, or the kind that the last of the coders makes (such as Votes, if "cases_to_votes" is the last). If "save" is set, it is saved with CourtData.save: whole, in a joblib file beside the table (such as "cases.joblib" beside "cases.csv"), and as the table. If "reuse" is true and it was saved before, the saved dataset is loaded instead (from the joblib file, or else from the table), and nothing is collected, parsed, or coded again.

def apply(self, item: amos.Dataset, **kwargs: Any) -> amos.Dataset:
    """Loads, codes, and saves the cases, as a dataset continuing `item`.

    Args:
        item: the dataset so far, whose seed and history are kept.
        **kwargs: "source", "coders", "save", "reuse", "label", "task", and
            "groups", and parameters for `load`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if there is no "source" and the loader has no default
            source.

    Returns:
        The dataset of the coded cases.

    """
    source = kwargs.pop('source', None) or self.default_source
    if source is None:
        message = (
            f'{self.name!r} has nothing to load: set its "source" in the '
            f'"{self.name}_parameters" section of the settings'
        )
        raise ValueError(message)
    label = kwargs.pop('label', None) or item.label
    task = kwargs.pop('task', None)
    groups = kwargs.pop('groups', None) or item.groups or None
    names = kwargs.pop('coders', self.default_coders)
    save = kwargs.pop('save', None)
    reuse = utilities.to_bool(kwargs.pop('reuse', False))
    saved = self._interim(save) if save else None
    reused = _reusable(saved) if saved is not None and reuse else None
    dataset: amos.Dataset
    if reused is not None:
        dataset = LoadCases().load(reused)
        dataset.seed = item.seed
        dataset.history = [*item.history, *dataset.history]
        dataset.record(
            self.name, source = str(source), reused = str(reused),
            rows = len(dataset.data), columns = len(dataset.data.columns))
    else:
        loaded = self.load(self._locate(source), **kwargs)
        if isinstance(loaded, amos.Dataset):
            dataset = loaded
            dataset.seed = item.seed
            dataset.history = [*item.history, *dataset.history]
        else:
            dataset = datasets.Cases(data = loaded, seed = item.seed)
            dataset.history = item.history
        dataset.record(
            self.name, source = str(source), rows = len(dataset.data),
            columns = len(dataset.data.columns))
        dataset = coders.code(dataset, names)
        if saved is not None and isinstance(dataset, datasets.CourtData):
            dataset.save(saved, clerk = self._get_clerk())
    return type(dataset).create(
        dataset, label = label, task = task, groups = groups)

def load(
    self,
    source: Any,
    *,
    batches: Any = None,
    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Divides any batches into the folder `source` and parses it.

    Args:
        source: the folder of Lexis-Nexis cases, found with the clerk.
        batches: files or folders of downloads of many cases, found with
            the clerk. The ".txt" files in a folder are used. Defaults to
            `None` (none).
        **kwargs: the parameters of `SourceLoader.load`.

    Returns:
        The table of parsed cases, labeled by "case_id".

    """
    folder = pathlib.Path(source)
    if batches:
        files = []
        for batch in utilities.listify(batches):
            found = self._locate(batch)
            files.extend(
                sorted(found.glob('*.txt')) if found.is_dir() else [found])
        lexis.split(files, folder)
    return super().load(folder, **kwargs)

Base class for techniques that load a table of reference data.

Reference data describes something other than parsed cases: the judges, the Supreme Court Database, the Integrated Database, or the political context of each year. Unlike a CaseLoader, a reference loader needs no "source". Like every loader, it starts a new dataset, so it usually begins a study whose rows are what the table describes (such as each justice's vote in each case). To add a table's columns to parsed cases, use a merger (such as add_scdb) instead.

def load(
    self,
    source: Any,
    *,
    download: Any = None,
    courts: Any = None,
    start_date: Any = None,
    end_date: Any = None,
    max_cases: Any = None,
    overwrite: Any = False,
    rulebooks: Any = None,
    keep_text: Any = False,
    limit: Any = None,
    workers: Any = None,
    **options: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Downloads the cases (if asked) and parses the folder `source`.

    Settings can be text (as a settings file gives them), so each is
    converted to the type it needs.

    Args:
        source: the folder of saved cases, found with the clerk.
        download: the name of a way to download, or "none". Defaults to
            `None` (none).
        courts: CourtListener court ids or groups to download. Defaults
            to `None`.
        start_date: earliest date filed to download (YYYY-MM-DD).
            Defaults to `None`.
        end_date: latest date filed to download (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults
            to `None`.
        max_cases: most cases to download. Defaults to `None` (every
            case).
        overwrite: whether to download cases that were already saved.
            Defaults to `False`.
        rulebooks: rules to parse with. Defaults to `None`, in which case
            `options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION` is used.
        keep_text: whether to keep the text of the cases' sections.
            Defaults to `False`.
        limit: most cases to parse. Defaults to `None` (every case).
        workers: number of processes to parse with. Defaults to `None`
            (one).
        **options: options of the way to download, such as "bulk_date".
            A folder or file that one names (such as "bulk_folder") is
            found with the clerk.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if "download" names no way to download, or one that
            saves cases of another source, or if no cases are found.

    Returns:
        The table of parsed cases, labeled by "case_id".

    """
    folder = pathlib.Path(source)
    if not utilities.is_none_setting(download):
        method = base.find_download(str(download))
        if method.source != self.reads:
            message = (
                f'the "{method.name}" download saves {method.source} '
                f'cases, but {self.name!r} reads {self.reads} cases')
            raise ValueError(message)
        method(locate = self._locate).download(
            folder,
            courts = utilities.expand_courts(courts) if courts else None,
            start_date = utilities.to_date(start_date),
            end_date = utilities.to_date(end_date),
            max_cases = utilities.to_integer(max_cases),
            overwrite = utilities.to_bool(overwrite),
            **options)
    return _parse(
        folder, self.reads, rulebooks = rulebooks,
        keep_text = keep_text, limit = limit, workers = workers)

docs.title: parsers
docs.text:
Turns saved court opinions into a table, one row for each case.

Parsing has three stages:

  1. A source (courtpy.sources.Source, such as CourtListener or Lexis-Nexis, or one that a study adds) reads each saved case into a Case with sections of text (such as "party", "judges", and "opinion") and information that needs no parsing (such as CourtListener's date filed).
  2. For Lexis-Nexis, the "lexis_nexis" rules find the sections of the header (see courtpy.lexis). CourtListener's sections come from its data.
  3. Rules find variables in the sections. The source's header rules (its header, such as "lexis_nexis_header": the parties, their roles, and the agencies among them, the court, the disposition, and the judges; see courtpy.rules.make_header_rules) and the "general" rules (the decision, procedure, and standards of review) are always applied, and then the rulebooks that are named (by default, the "federal" rules, which add citations, civil (with tort, contract, and intellectual property), constitutional, and criminal issues, and agencies; "citations", "civil", "constitutional", "criminal", and "agencies" can be named alone). Each rulebook has the rules of its "general" file and then those of its "federal" file, if there is one (see courtpy.rules).

The rulebooks are those of amos (amos.parsers.Rulebook, and courtpy's own in courtpy.rules), which search a table of the sections of many cases at once, a row for each case and a column for each section.

Every section except those whose names end in "_lines" is collapsed onto one line between stages 2 and 3, so that phrases broken across lines are found.

With "keep_text", the table keeps the text of every section, so that parse_all (ParseAll) can parse the cases again after the rules change, without reading the saved files again.

Contents

ParseAll: finds information in text with rules, or parses cases again from their kept text with every rulebook that fits them. Parser: parses cases with rulebooks. find_files: returns the saved cases of a source in a folder. parse: parses a folder of saved cases into a table. logger: the module's logger, which reports parsing progress and cases that could not be parsed.

Bases: ParseAll

Finds information in text with rules, or parses cases again.

This is amos's parse_all, which it replaces in the amos library: given "rules", it applies them as amos.parsers.ParseAll does. Given none, it parses the cases of a table again from the text of their sections, which the table has if they were loaded with "keep_text" (such as after a change to the rules). Each case is parsed with every rulebook that fits it: the header rules of its source (by its "source" column; see courtpy.sources.Source), the rules of options._REQUIRED_RULEBOOKS, and "rulebooks" (by default, those of the jurisdiction, options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION). Then "author", "panel_size", "concurrences", "dissents", and "word_count" are made again.

A value that the rules find replaces the table's. Where the rules find nothing, the table's value is kept, such as a CourtListener case's court from CourtListener's id for it.

    *,
    rules: Any = None,

    **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:

            rulebook that fits them.

@classmethod
def create(
    cls,
    rulebooks: str | pathlib.Path | Sequence[str | pathlib.Path] = (
        options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION),
    *,
    keep_text: bool = False) -> Parser:
    """Returns a parser with the rules in `rulebooks`.

    The rules of `options._REQUIRED_RULEBOOKS` are always applied first
    (after the header rules of each case's source), whether or not they
    are named.

    Args:
        rulebooks: names of rulebooks (such as "federal" or "civil") or
            paths to CSV files or folders of them, applied in order.
            Defaults to `options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION`.
        keep_text: whether to keep the text of the cases' sections in the
            table. Defaults to `False`.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if a rulebook is not the name of one, a CSV
            file, or a folder with CSV files.
        ValueError: if a file is missing a column or a row is not a valid
            rule. The message names the file and row.

    Returns:
        The parser.

    """
    if isinstance(rulebooks, str):
        rulebooks = utilities.listify(rulebooks)
    elif isinstance(rulebooks, pathlib.Path):
        rulebooks = [rulebooks]
    rulebook = amos.parsers.Rulebook.create(
        *options._REQUIRED_RULEBOOKS, *rulebooks)
    return cls(rulebook = rulebook, keep_text = keep_text)

def parse(self, case: cases.Case) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns one row of the table for `case`.

    Args:
        case: the case to parse.

    return {
        str(k): None if _is_missing(v) else v for k, v in row.items()}

def parse_cases(self, found: Sequence[cases.Case]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns a table of `found`, with a row for each case.

    The cases of each source are parsed together, with every rule
    searching every case at once.

    Args:
        found: the cases to parse.

    Returns:
        The table, with a row for each case, in order, labeled 0, 1, 2,
            and so on. Information from a case's `metadata` comes first
            and is used instead of any variable of the same name that the
            rules find (unless it is missing).

    """
    groups: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for position, case in enumerate(found):
        groups.setdefault(case.source, []).append(position)
    tables = [
        self._parse_source([found[p] for p in positions]).set_axis(
            positions)
        for positions in groups.values()]
    if not tables:
        return pd.DataFrame()
    return pd.concat(tables).sort_index() if len(tables) > 1 else tables[0]

The table, labeled by each case's id ("case_id"). A case that cannot be read is left out, with a warning.

Source code in src/courtpy/wrangler/parsers.py 
def parse(
    files: pathlib.Path | str | Iterable[pathlib.Path | str],
    source: str = 'courtlistener',
    rulebooks: str | pathlib.Path | Sequence[str | pathlib.Path] = (
        options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION),
    *,
    keep_text: bool = False,
    limit: int | None = None,
    workers: int = 1) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Parses saved cases into a table, one row for each case.

    Columns with several values in a case (such as "panel_judges" and
    "citations_case") are text, with "; " between the values. The
    `split_values` technique (`coders.SplitValues`) turns them into lists or
    into a column for each value.

    Args:
        files: a folder of saved cases (searched with its subfolders), or the
            paths of saved cases.
        source: the name of the source the cases came from, such as
            "courtlistener" (the default) or "lexis_nexis" (see
            `courtpy.sources.SOURCES`).
        rulebooks: names of rulebooks (such as "federal") or paths to CSV
            files or folders of them. Defaults to
            `options._DEFAULT_JURISDICTION`.
        keep_text: whether to keep the text of the cases' sections in the
            table (see `ParseAll`). Defaults to `False`.
        limit: most cases to parse, for trying out rules. Defaults to `None`
            (every case).
        workers: number of processes to parse with. Defaults to 1.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if there is no source named `source`.

    Returns:
        The table, labeled by each case's id ("case_id"). A case that cannot
            be read is left out, with a warning.

    """
    reader = base.find_source(source)
    if isinstance(files, str | pathlib.Path):
        paths = reader.find_files(files)
    else:
        paths = [pathlib.Path(p) for p in files]
    if limit is not None:
        paths = paths[:limit]
    parser = Parser.create(rulebooks, keep_text = keep_text)
    labels: list[str] = []
    tables: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    failures = 0
    outcomes: list[Any] = []
    for chunk_outcomes, table in _parse_all(parser, paths, reader, workers):
        outcomes.extend(chunk_outcomes)
        tables.append(table)
    taken: set[str] = set()
    for path, outcome in zip(paths, outcomes, strict = True):
        if isinstance(outcome, BaseException):
            failures += 1
            logger.warning('%s could not be parsed: %s', path, outcome)
            continue
        unique, number = outcome, 1
        while unique in taken:
            number += 1
            unique = f'{outcome}_{number}'
        taken.add(unique)
        labels.append(unique)
    logger.info(
        'parsed %d cases (%d could not be parsed)', len(labels), failures)
    tables = [t for t in tables if not t.empty]
    data = pd.concat(tables, ignore_index = True) if tables else pd.DataFrame()
    data.index = pd.Index(labels, name = 'case_id')
    return cases.tidy(data)

docs.title: rules
docs.text:
courtpy's rulebooks, which find information in the text of court opinions.

The rules are rows of CSV files (spreadsheets) in courtpy's "instructions" folder, so they can be read and changed without knowing Python. They are amos rulebooks: each row is a rule of amos.parsers.ParseAll, which documents the columns and kinds of rules (and also reads files in the older layout, with "target", "variable", "label", and "section").

The rules of each topic (such as "criminal") are in two places. The file in the "general" folder has the rules that fit opinions of any jurisdiction, and the file of the same name in a jurisdiction's folder (such as "federal") has the rules that fit only that jurisdiction, if there are any. A rulebook for a topic applies the general rules and then the jurisdiction's (see find_rule_files). courtpy reads only federal cases so far, so every rulebook here is federal.

Each source's rules are in its folder of "sources" (such as "sources/lexis_nexis"): the rules that find the sections of its cases, with a file for each kind of court (such as "federal_appellate.csv"; see find_structure_file), and the rules of its header ("header.csv"). The header rulebook of a source (see make_header_rules) applies "general/header.csv" (the rules that fit every source), rules made from the jurisdiction's "agencies.csv" that find the agencies named in each party and the history (see make_agency_rules), the source's "header.csv", and, for a source whose cases name their court in text, rules made from the jurisdiction's "courts.csv" that find "court_num" and "court_name" (see make_court_rules). Rules made from "courts.csv" also find the court whose decision is reviewed in every source's history ("lower_court_num" and "lower_court_name"). So the header rules name no courts or agencies of their own, and a court or agency added to the tables is found without changing them.

register_rulebooks makes a rulebook of each topic, a subclass of amos.parsers.ParseAll that is added to the amos library, so it has a name that courtpy.parse, the "rulebooks" of a case loader, other rulebooks, and the "rules" of parse_all can use (such as "federal" or "civil"). Each is also a technique of its own (such as parse_civil), which searches the columns of text of a dataset (such as "opinion", which a case loader keeps with "keep_text"). A study can make rulebooks of its own folders of rules the same way. courtpy's own are in RULEBOOKS: "general", "citations", "civil", "constitutional", "criminal", "review", "agencies", "federal" (all of those, in that order), the header rulebooks "header" (for a source with no rules of its own), "courtlistener_header", and "lexis_nexis_header", and "lexis_nexis", which finds the sections of a Lexis-Nexis case. The parser applies a source's header rulebook (named by its header) before the others.

Rules that make several values in one cell (names, matches, and categories rules, such as "panel_judges", "citations_case", and "agencies") separate them with "; ", so that a table of cases can be saved as a CSV file. The split_values technique (coders.SplitValues) turns such text into lists or columns.

Contents

Rulebooks

courtpy's rulebooks, by their names. case_type_prefixes: returns the prefixes of the names of the rules of the topics of cases, each of which is a case type. find_rule_files: returns the files of rules of a topic in a jurisdiction. find_structure_file: returns the file of rules that finds the sections of a source's cases. make_agency_rules: returns rules that find the agencies named in sections of the header. make_court_rules: returns rules that find a case's court from its name. make_header_rules: returns the rules of a source's header. register_rulebooks: makes a rulebook of each topic in folders of rule files. _AGENCY_COLUMNS: the sections of the header whose agencies are found. _PARTY_AGENCY_END: what must follow an agency's name in a party. _PARTY_COLUMNS: the sections of the header that are parties. _CASE_TYPE_TOPICS: the topics whose rules' prefixes are case types. _COURT_NAME_COLUMNS: the columns of a table of courts with patterns of their names, in the order they are tried. _GENERAL: the folder of the rules that fit every jurisdiction. _HEADER: the stem of the files of header rules. _LOWER_COURT_LEVELS: the levels of courts, in the order they are tried, that the history is searched for to find the court whose decision is reviewed. _INSTRUCTIONS: courtpy's "instructions" folder. _JURISDICTION: the jurisdiction of the cases that courtpy reads. _SOURCES: the folder of the rules of each source. _TOPICS: the topics of courtpy's rules, in the order of the "federal" rulebook.

Each rule of the "criminal", "civil", and "constitutional" files names a column with a prefix (such as "criminal" in "criminal_firearm", or "tort" in "tort_negligence"), and each prefix is a case type (see code_case_type). A prefix added to a file (such as "immigration_") is a case type too.

def case_type_prefixes(
    jurisdiction: str | None = _JURISDICTION) -> list[str]:
    """Returns the prefixes of the rules of the topics of cases.

    Each rule of the "criminal", "civil", and "constitutional" files names a
    column with a prefix (such as "criminal" in "criminal_firearm", or "tort"
    in "tort_negligence"), and each prefix is a case type (see
    `code_case_type`). A prefix added to a file (such as "immigration_") is
    a case type too.

    Args:
        jurisdiction: the folder of the jurisdiction's rules, such as
            "federal". Defaults to `_JURISDICTION`. If it is `None`, only
            the general rules are read.

    Returns:
        The prefixes, in the order in which they first appear in the files.

    """
    prefixes: dict[str, None] = {}
    for topic in _CASE_TYPE_TOPICS:
        for path in find_rule_files(topic, jurisdiction):
            names = utilities.read_csv(path, usecols = ['name'])['name']
            for name in names.dropna().astype(str):
                prefix, separator, _ = name.strip().partition('_')
                if separator and prefix:
                    prefixes.setdefault(prefix)
    return list(prefixes)

def find_rule_files(
    topic: str,
    jurisdiction: str | None = _JURISDICTION) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Returns the files of rules of a topic in a jurisdiction.

    Args:
        topic: the stem of the files, such as "criminal".
        jurisdiction: the folder of the jurisdiction's rules, such as
            "federal". Defaults to `_JURISDICTION`. If it is `None`, only
            the general rules are returned.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if neither the "general" folder nor the
            jurisdiction's folder has a file for the topic.

    Returns:
        The file in the "general" folder and then the file in the
            jurisdiction's folder, leaving out either one that does not
            exist (as "federal/citations.csv" does not, since every rule of
            citations fits every jurisdiction).

    """
    folders = [_GENERAL]
    if jurisdiction is not None:
        folders.append(_INSTRUCTIONS / jurisdiction)
    files = [
        folder / f'{topic}.csv' for folder in folders
        if (folder / f'{topic}.csv').is_file()]
    if not files:
        searched = ', '.join(str(folder) for folder in folders)
        message = f'there is no file of rules for {topic!r} in {searched}'
        raise FileNotFoundError(message)
    return files

def find_structure_file(source: str, courts: str) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Returns the file of rules that finds the sections of a source's cases.

    Args:
        source: the name of the source, which is also the name of its folder
            of rules in `_SOURCES`, such as "lexis_nexis".
        courts: the kind of courts whose cases the rules fit, which is the
            stem of the file, such as "federal_appellate".

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if there is no such file.

    Returns:
        The path of the file.

    """
    path = _SOURCES / source / f'{courts}.csv'
    if not path.is_file():
        message = f'there are no rules for {courts!r} cases of {source!r}'
        raise FileNotFoundError(message)
    return path

Returns rules that find the agencies named in sections of the header.

Each rule of the jurisdiction's "agencies" files (see find_rule_files) is made into a rule for each of columns, which searches only that column and makes "{column}_agencies" (such as "party1_agencies"), so that the header names no agencies of its own. In a column of party_columns, an agency's name must end a party (see _PARTY_AGENCY_END), so that a company or person named for an agency is not taken for it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default jurisdiction str | None

the folder of the jurisdiction's rules, such as "federal". Defaults to _JURISDICTION. If it is None, only the general rules are read.

_JURISDICTION columns Sequence[str]

the sections to search. Defaults to _AGENCY_COLUMNS ("party1", "party2", and "history").

_AGENCY_COLUMNS party_columns Sequence[str]

the sections of columns that are parties. Defaults to _PARTY_COLUMNS ("party1" and "party2").

_PARTY_COLUMNS

Returns:

Type Description list[dict[str, Any]]

The rules, as dicts with the columns of a file of rules, ordered by column and then by the order of the files. They are empty if there are no "agencies" files.

Source code in src/courtpy/wrangler/rules.py 
def make_agency_rules(
    jurisdiction: str | None = _JURISDICTION,
    columns: Sequence[str] = _AGENCY_COLUMNS,
    party_columns: Sequence[str] = _PARTY_COLUMNS) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Returns rules that find the agencies named in sections of the header.

    Each rule of the jurisdiction's "agencies" files (see `find_rule_files`)
    is made into a rule for each of `columns`, which searches only that
    column and makes "{column}_agencies" (such as "party1_agencies"), so
    that the header names no agencies of its own. In a column of
    `party_columns`, an agency's name must end a party (see
    `_PARTY_AGENCY_END`), so that a company or person named for an agency is
    not taken for it.

    Args:
        jurisdiction: the folder of the jurisdiction's rules, such as
            "federal". Defaults to `_JURISDICTION`. If it is `None`, only
            the general rules are read.
        columns: the sections to search. Defaults to `_AGENCY_COLUMNS`
            ("party1", "party2", and "history").
        party_columns: the sections of `columns` that are parties. Defaults
            to `_PARTY_COLUMNS` ("party1" and "party2").

    Returns:
        The rules, as `dict`s with the columns of a file of rules, ordered by
            column and then by the order of the files. They are empty if
            there are no "agencies" files.

    """
    try:
        paths = find_rule_files('agencies', jurisdiction)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    tables = [
        utilities.read_csv(path, dtype = str, keep_default_na = False)
        for path in paths]
    made: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for column in columns:
        for table in tables:
            for row in table.to_dict('records'):
                rule = {str(key): value for key, value in row.items()}
                rule.update(column = column, name = f'{column}_agencies')
                if column in party_columns:
                    rule['pattern'] = (
                        f'(?:{rule["pattern"]}){_PARTY_AGENCY_END}')
                made.append(rule)
    return made
